za.headline: Safa Delays Coach Hire as Afcon Qualifiers Approach
za.dek: The South African Football Association has not yet named a successor to Hugo Broos, with the national team's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers set to begin in September.
paragraphs: The South African Football Association (Safa) faces a critical juncture as the national team, Bafana Bafana, prepares to commence its 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign without a formally appointed head coach. The departure of Hugo Broos after a five-year tenure has left a vacancy that Safa has yet to fill, despite knowing for months that the Belgian coach would not continue.

Bafana Bafana are scheduled to begin their quest for a third consecutive Afcon appearance on September 23, with matches against Guinea and Eritrea. Further qualifiers are set for November against Kenya. Safa's technical committee chairperson, Jack Maluleke, indicated in May that the search for Broos's successor was underway, acknowledging the need for continuity post-World Cup.

Reports in July suggested Safa had attempted to retain Broos for another year following the team's qualification for their first World Cup in sixteen years. However, Broos, citing his age and desire to be closer to his family in Belgium, had indicated the Bafana Bafana role would likely be his last coaching position.

za.headline: Creators Seek Power Beyond Brand Deals
za.dek: South Africa's digital content creators are pushing for greater economic control as their influence grows in the attention economy.
paragraphs: South Africa's creator economy is rapidly expanding, fostering new businesses and opportunities for young entrepreneurs. However, a significant shift is underway as creators demand more economic power, moving beyond reliance on brand partnerships and platform-controlled monetization systems.

Creators are increasingly becoming the new broadcasters, attracting large audiences and wielding considerable influence over digital culture. This rise in influence is prompting calls for creators to have a larger stake in the value generated by the audiences they cultivate, drawing parallels to the established commercial structures of traditional media.

To achieve greater economic leverage, creators are urged to organize and present a united front when negotiating with major technology companies like TikTok and Meta. A collective voice is seen as crucial for implementing real change and influencing industry policies, rather than individual creators approaching these platforms alone.

za.headline: TEEKS's South African Tour Connects Indigenous Roots to Soul Music
za.dek: Māori soul singer TEEKS explores the sacred space of live performance and acknowledges Africa's foundational role in soul music during his debut tour.
paragraphs: Māori soul singer TEEKS, real name Te Karehana Gardiner-Toi, is performing in South Africa for the first time this week. His music, deeply influenced by his Māori heritage, resonates with South African audiences who have embraced his introspective soul tracks like "First Time" and "Remember Me." TEEKS views live performance as a sacred space for healing and a reciprocal exchange of energy, a concept he feels aligns with South Africa's rich cultural tapestry.

The artist highlighted the importance of acknowledging the origins of soul music, stating that its roots lie in Africa and have profoundly influenced global genres. He believes his connection to his heritage and ancestral lineage informs his approach to songwriting and navigating the music industry. This self-awareness, he suggests, allows him to honor traditions and move through life with a strong sense of identity.

TEEKS expressed anticipation for discovering synergies within South Africa's diverse culture, drawing parallels between his own indigenous lineage and the continent's rich history. He views the global benefit derived from soul music and black culture as a significant conversation, recognizing Africa's foundational contribution to genres that have shaped the world.

ng.headline: Yari claims APC dominance beyond 2031, opposition reacts
ng.dek: Senator Abdul’Aziz Yari’s projection of the ruling party’s power beyond 2027 has drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties.
paragraphs: Senator Abdul’Aziz Yari, newly appointed Director-General of President Bola Tinubu’s Presidential Campaign Council, has stated that the All Progressives Congress (APC) will remain in power beyond 2031. Yari made the declaration at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja, a day after his appointment. This statement goes beyond typical campaign rhetoric by projecting the APC's dominance over a longer political horizon, which has prompted swift and strong reactions from opposition parties.

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) have responded to Yari's claim. PDP National Publicity Secretary, Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, urged Yari to focus on his mandate of securing President Tinubu's re-election in 2027 before discussing the party's future beyond that year. The PDP's stance is to reject the premise that the opposition is already out of contention and that the election's outcome is predetermined.

APC governors, led by Hope Uzodinma, have committed to securing President Tinubu's re-election in their respective states for the 2027 general election. This commitment from within the ruling party reinforces the campaign's focus on the upcoming election cycle. The political environment is shaped by perceptions of strength, which can influence the decisions of politicians, potential defectors, financiers, and aspirants.

ng.headline: NFF Appoints New NPFL Chief Operating Officer Amid Reforms
ng.dek: Dr Ayo Abdulrahaman takes immediate charge of the Nigeria Premier Football League's daily operations as part of wider restructuring efforts.
paragraphs: The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has appointed Dr Ayo Abdulrahaman as the new Chief Operating Officer (COO) of the Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL), effective immediately. This appointment marks a significant step in the NFF's reform agenda, following the mass resignation of its leadership and the suspension of its elective congress. The move aims to ensure continuity in football administration while broader structural changes are implemented.

Abdulrahaman, who holds a doctorate in sports administration and possesses extensive experience across Nigerian leagues, will oversee the NPFL's day-to-day operations. The NFF's interim general secretary, Dr Emmanuel Ikpeme, stated that this appointment aligns with a directive for non-NFF staff in leadership roles to vacate their positions. This interim measure is designed to stabilize domestic competitions during the ongoing reform process.

The appointment comes as the 2026/27 NPFL season commences, amidst calls for improved league administration, commercialization, and professional standards. Abdulrahaman's immediate focus will be on managing league operations and contributing to the development of a more efficient and commercially viable domestic football structure. The NFF seeks to address long-standing governance and developmental challenges within Nigerian football.

et.headline: Ethiopian Airlines Adds Direct Freighter Route to Chengdu, China
et.dek: The airline's cargo division launched a new direct freighter service connecting Addis Ababa with Chengdu, China, enhancing its Asian network.
paragraphs: Ethiopian Airlines has initiated a new direct freighter service between Addis Ababa and Chengdu, China, expanding its cargo operations in Asia. The airline's cargo and logistics business announced the service on Friday, establishing a direct cargo link between Africa and China. The inaugural flight was met with a ceremony and water cannon salute upon arrival in Chengdu, the capital of Sichuan province.

The new air link is expected to significantly boost trade and economic exchanges between western China and Africa, according to Ethiopian Cargo and Logistics services. China is a crucial market for Ethiopian, which operates the largest cargo network in Africa. This Chengdu service follows the addition of Urumqi to the airline's Chinese cargo network last year.

Ethiopian Airlines currently operates over 190 weekly flights to 27 Asian destinations, including 83 weekly flights to 11 cities in China. With a fleet of more than 145 modern aircraft and advanced cargo infrastructure, the airline transports nearly one million tons of cargo annually to over 145 global destinations.

et.headline: Enat Bank Registers Nearly 6.8 Million Shares with Regulators
et.dek: The Ethiopian Capital Market Authority has officially approved the registration of 6,785,310 existing shares held by Enat Bank shareholders.
paragraphs: Enat Bank Share Company has received official approval from the Ethiopian Capital Market Authority (ECMA) for the registration of close to 6.8 million existing shares. The nation's capital market regulator issued a public notice on August 27, 2026, confirming its approval of Enat's securities registration statement.

The registration, formalized under the Public Offer and Trading of Securities Directive No. 1030/2024, covers a total of 6,785,310 shares previously held by shareholders. ECMA stated that the notice serves solely to inform the public and should not be interpreted as an endorsement or solicitation for buying or selling securities.

This action aligns with the directive's requirement for all securities offered, sold, or previously issued to the public to be registered with the Authority, unless specifically exempted. This process aims to enhance transparency and regulatory oversight as Ethiopia's capital market continues to develop.

et.headline: Sudanese Army Shoots Down Drone Near Ethiopian Border
et.dek: The Sudanese army reported downing an unmanned aerial vehicle that had crossed into the country from the direction of Ethiopia.
paragraphs: The Sudanese army announced on Thursday that it shot down an "enemy strategic drone" that entered its airspace from Ethiopia. The military's General Command stated the drone was downed in the morning north of Sarkam in Sudan’s Blue Nile state, which borders Ethiopia.

This incident follows an earlier report this month where the Sudanese army claimed to have shot down three FH-95 drones in North Kordofan state. The army described the downed aircraft as a "strategic" unmanned vehicle but offered no further specifics on its capabilities or origin.

Blue Nile State remains a strategically significant region amidst the ongoing conflict between Sudan’s army and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The conflict, which began in April 2023, has resulted in tens of thousands of deaths and displaced approximately 13 million people, according to UN and international estimates.

gh.headline: Ghanaian Hospital Fails Lead to Maternal Deaths
gh.dek: A grieving husband points to systemic failures and negligence after his wife died during a scheduled C-section.
paragraphs: Theresa Boakye Dua, 31, died at Ridge Hospital in Accra during a scheduled Caesarean section, leaving her husband devastated and angry. He believes negligence and unprofessional conduct within the healthcare system contributed to her death. Her husband has vowed to reveal the full truth, stating this tragedy is about preventing similar losses for other families and questioning why preventable maternal deaths persist in Ghana.

The Deputy Minister of Health, Dr. Grace Ayensu-Danquah, recently highlighted maternal mortality as Ghana's worst-performing health indicator. In 2025, the country recorded approximately 945 institutional maternal deaths. She emphasized that the Ministry of Health cannot address this crisis alone and called for a new approach to tackle the problem effectively.

Theresa's story has resonated on social media, prompting others to share their own difficult childbirth experiences, including delays in care and the loss of loved ones. These shared narratives collectively illustrate a maternal health crisis that extends beyond statistics, representing individual lives, families, and profound grief.

gh.headline: Landlady Recalls Hijacker's Friendly Demeanor
gh.dek: A former property manager recounts her interactions with a man now accused of facilitating the 9/11 attacks.
paragraphs: Holly Ratchford, who managed the Parkwood Apartments in San Diego, California, in the late 1990s, has spoken about her past interactions with Omar al-Bayoumi. Al-Bayoumi, a Saudi national, is alleged to have provided support to Nawaf al-Hazmi and Khalid al-Mihdhar, two of the hijackers involved in the September 11, 2001 attacks. Ratchford described Bayoumi as friendly and sociable, recalling his participation in pool parties and his family's invitations for meals.

Ratchford stated that Bayoumi, who lived at the complex with his family from September 1999, introduced her to the two men who would later become hijackers. She expressed disbelief and ongoing struggle to reconcile the seemingly ordinary neighbor with his alleged role in the attacks. Her testimony is part of a $1 trillion lawsuit filed by victims' families against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, though the kingdom and Bayoumi deny the allegations.

The federal judge in the 9/11 families' lawsuit found a year ago that evidence supported a reasonable inference of coordination between Bayoumi, a Saudi diplomat, and the Saudi government in assisting the hijackers. This ruling allowed the case to proceed, despite Saudi Arabia's appeal. Ratchford has provided a sealed declaration to the court but had not previously spoken publicly about her experiences.

gh.headline: Ghana Tourism Creates Over 24,000 New Jobs in One Year
gh.dek: The tourism sector's expansion has led to significant job growth, with new programs aiming to train young professionals.
paragraphs: Ghana's tourism industry is increasingly becoming a key source of employment and skills development for young people. Between 2021 and 2022, tourism-related jobs grew by more than 24,000, reaching 276,985 positions. By 2023, direct employment in hotels, restaurants, travel agencies, and other tourism enterprises stood at approximately 204,591. When including indirect jobs in supporting industries like handicrafts, the total employment figure for 2023 was estimated at 429,641.

The sector's growth continued into 2024, with Ghana recording 1,288,804 international tourist arrivals and a rise in licensed tourism enterprises from 5,786 to 6,702. This expansion generated about US$4.8 billion in revenue, increasing demand for workers across various services. In 2025, international arrivals saw a further increase to 1,306,962, reinforcing the market for tourism businesses and creating more employment and entrepreneurial opportunities.

To further support youth employment, the Ghana Tourism Authority and Ghana Tourism Federation are launching initiatives like the Graduate Tourism Employment and Mobility (GTEM) Programme. This program will train and certify 200 graduates as professional tour guides, deploying them to various tourism establishments and providing mobility support to help them start their own businesses.

gh.headline: SankofaFresh Cuts Food Waste, Connects Farmers to Markets
gh.dek: Ghanaian technology platform SankofaFresh uses data and cold-chain monitoring to reduce post-harvest losses and improve market access for smallholder farmers.
paragraphs: Ghanaian food-systems technology platform SankofaFresh is working to reduce post-harvest losses and connect smallholder farmers to more reliable markets. The platform uses technology to improve how fresh produce is monitored, stored, and connected to buyers. Leehouse and Chemical Ventures, a food manufacturing company in Ghana, has adopted SankofaFresh, which has helped reduce losses and create more dependable market opportunities for farmers.

SankofaFresh was co-founded by Rhoda Osei-Nkwantabisa, Joshua Kojo Aduampong Mantey, George Arthur, and Rosemary Agbzo. Joshua Mantey leads the platform’s data and artificial intelligence systems for cold-chain monitoring and farmer-to-market matching. His PhD research at Northeastern University involves large-scale computational modeling and machine learning, an approach applied to SankofaFresh's technology to boost efficiency and cut waste across the agricultural value chain.

The platform's efforts to reduce post-harvest losses and strengthen market access for smallholder farmers earned it the Audience Choice Award at the World Bank Group Youth Summit Pitch Competition in 2026. SankofaFresh positions technology, data, and market connections as vital tools for ensuring that more food grown by farmers reaches consumers and businesses, contributing to food security and nutrition in Ghana and beyond.

cd.headline: UN Chief Denounces Ebola Indifference Amidst DRC Outbreak
cd.dek: António Guterres calls for urgent international action against the largest Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo's history.
paragraphs: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres has issued an urgent appeal to the global community to intensify efforts against the ongoing Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo. He characterized the international response as suffering from a "virus of indifference," highlighting the severity of the outbreak, which is now the most significant in the nation's recorded history. The call comes as health officials grapple with containment and treatment strategies.

The epidemic's scale necessitates a robust and coordinated international response, Guterres stated, emphasizing that the "virus of indifference" hinders effective containment. While the primary focus remains on the health crisis, separate reports from South Kivu's Kitutu village highlight persistent security concerns. Civil society there is denouncing the continued presence of military personnel and Wazalendo fighters in mining sites, a situation that persists despite a presidential order for their withdrawal.

This persistent presence of armed groups in mining areas, particularly in the Mwenga territory of South Kivu, raises concerns about stability and the potential for further conflict or disruption. The situation in Kitutu, where military forces remain in mining zones a month after President Félix Tshisekedi's directive for their removal, underscores ongoing challenges in implementing presidential orders and maintaining security in resource-rich regions.

cd.headline: UNC Deputies Pledge Support for National Dialogue
cd.dek: Lawmakers from the A/A UNC and AVK 2018 political groups met in Kinshasa to affirm their commitment to the president's national dialogue initiative.
paragraphs: Deputies from the A/A UNC and AVK 2018 political groups met in Kinshasa on Friday, August 29, following President Félix Tshisekedi's announcement of a national dialogue. The lawmakers gathered at the Palais du peuple to discuss the country's political situation and reaffirmed their support for the initiative, expressing a strong willingness to participate actively in the upcoming discussions.

The elected officials are calling on all vital forces of the nation, including political actors, civil society, traditional leaders, religious confessions, women's organizations, and youth groups, to support this process. They emphasized the importance of prioritizing the nation's superior interest, national cohesion, and the pursuit of lasting peace, all while respecting the Democratic Republic of Congo's sovereignty and territorial integrity.

cd.headline: DRC, Tanzania, UNHCR Plan Refugee Returns
cd.dek: A tripartite commission agreed to facilitate voluntary repatriation of Congolese refugees from Tanzania based on resource availability and safe zones.
paragraphs: A joint commission involving the Democratic Republic of Congo, Tanzania, and the UNHCR has outlined a plan for the voluntary return of Congolese refugees residing in Tanzania. The eighth edition of the tripartite commission, held in Lubumbashi, concluded with an agreement to progressively repatriate refugees who wish to return to the DRC. This process will be implemented based on the availability of resources and the establishment of appropriate reception facilities.

The commission emphasized that all returns must be voluntary and free from pressure. Repatriation will be facilitated to areas identified by the Congolese government as safe, accessible, and suitable for sustainable reintegration. The UNHCR representative in the DRC, Patrick Kirya, noted that insecurity in parts of North Kivu, South Kivu, and Ituri currently prevents safe returns to these regions, and such returns are not encouraged.

The Congolese government, through the Vice Prime Minister and Minister of Interior, Jacquemain Shabani, assured that efforts are underway to create favorable conditions for the reception of returning refugees. The government is committed to facilitating the return of its citizens living in Tanzania, working to establish the necessary infrastructure and security measures for their reintegration.

paragraphs: The territory of Popokabaka, located in the Kwango province of the Democratic Republic of Congo, has not yet recovered from the occupation by Mobondo militiamen. Three months after their evacuation from villages where they had entrenched themselves, the region continues to bear the scars of their presence. The economic infrastructure is in ruins, and the livelihoods of residents have been severely impacted.

The aftermath of the Mobondo militia's presence includes widespread destruction. Livestock has been damaged, and agricultural fields vandalized, directly affecting the local food supply and the primary source of income for many families. The economic activities in the area have come to a standstill, leaving residents struggling to rebuild their lives and their community.

The lingering effects of the Mobondo phenomenon continue to plague Popokabaka. The violation of young girls and the overall devastation have left deep, unhealed wounds on the community. Efforts to restore normalcy and rebuild the shattered economy are ongoing, but the path to recovery remains long and arduous for the affected population.

Three months after their evacuation from villages where they had entrenched themselves, the region continues to bear the scars of their presence. The economic infrastructure is in ruins, and the livelihoods of residents have been severely impacted.

The aftermath of the Mobondo militia's presence includes widespread destruction. Livestock has been damaged, and agricultural fields vandalized, directly affecting the local food supply and the primary source of income for many families. The economic activities in the area have come to a standstill, leaving residents struggling to rebuild their lives and their community.

The lingering effects of the Mobondo phenomenon continue to plague Popokabaka. The violation of young girls and the overall devastation have left deep, unhealed wounds on the community. Efforts to restore normalcy and rebuild the shattered economy are ongoing, but the path to recovery remains long and arduous for the affected population.

tz.headline: Tanzania Ruling Party Expels Vice President After Resignation
tz.dek: Emmanuel Nchimbi's departure from his vice presidential post is followed by expulsion from the ruling CCM party, deepening political rifts.
paragraphs: Vice President Emmanuel Nchimbi resigned on August 25, 2026, a move followed swiftly by his expulsion from Tanzania's ruling CCM party for disciplinary and ethical violations. This sequence of events, occurring after Nchimbi's resignation letter appeared online and was accepted by President Samia, suggests a fallout within the party leadership. The party's decision contrasts with Nchimbi's stated intention to retire from public service, highlighting internal schisms.

Nchimbi's resignation and subsequent expulsion echo historical political departures within Tanzania, notably Aboud Jumbe's exit four decades prior, who relinquished multiple high-profile positions. Jumbe's departure was linked to his support for a three-government Union structure during the 'Crisis of the Union' period. The recent events also follow the suspension of the investigative newspaper Mwanahalisi for reporting Nchimbi's resistance to pressure to resign due to disagreements with the President.

The vice-presidency in Tanzania is often seen as a largely ceremonial role, though constitutionally empowered to assist with Union matters and act in the President's absence. However, the position holds potential for succession, as demonstrated in 2021. Nchimbi's situation, marked by his expulsion from the CCM party, further tests Tanzania's reputation for peace and stability amidst these internal political developments.

tz.headline: Tanzania Health Summit to Convene 2,000 Delegates
tz.dek: The 13th Tanzania Health Summit will focus on improving health systems and building health sovereignty with over 70 exhibitions and 40 forums.
paragraphs: Over 2,000 delegates are expected at the 13th Tanzania Health Summit (THS) in Dar es Salaam from October 5 to 7, focusing on improving health systems under the theme “Building Health Sovereignty and Strengthening Health Systems in a Changing Global Order.” The event will bring together government leaders, healthcare professionals, policymakers, entrepreneurs, and young change-makers from more than 25 countries.

The summit will feature over 70 exhibitions and 40 institutional forums, alongside the THS Health Workers Awards, Youth Capacity Building programs, and CHIA Innovation Awards. THS President Dr. Omary Chillo emphasized the event's importance in empowering nations to break foreign dependency, control medical supplies, and build self-sufficient healthcare systems resilient to shocks.

The THS is recognized as a leading Public Private Health Platform, having convened over 10,000 stakeholders from more than 230 institutions in its 12-year history. It has contributed to reforms like the Universal Health Insurance Act and Integrated Community Health Workers Programs, showcasing over one thousand research studies. Organizations like JICA and Ifakara Health Institute will present projects at this year's summit.

tz.headline: Attorney General Affirms Ndejembi's Vice Presidency
tz.dek: The Attorney General explained the constitutional procedures followed in appointing Deogratius Ndejembi as Vice-President after a resignation.
paragraphs: Attorney General Hamza Johari stated in the National Assembly that Deogratius Ndejembi's appointment as Vice-President followed Tanzania's 1977 Constitution. The assembly had endorsed Ndejembi following Ambassador Emmanuel Nchimbi’s resignation. Johari explained that President Samia Suluhu Hassan nominated Ndejembi, with the nomination submitted to the National Assembly. The process adhered to constitutional and legal requirements for filling a vacant Vice-Presidential office.

Johari clarified that the effective date of a resignation is when the letter is received or a specified future date. He cited Article 50(4) of the Constitution, which mandates the President to appoint a successor within 14 days of a vacancy caused by removal, death, or resignation. This appointment must then be confirmed by the National Assembly through a majority vote. The Attorney General emphasized that constitutional provisions should be interpreted harmoniously, not in isolation.

Addressing legal interpretations, Johari referred to Article 47(4), which outlines qualifications for holding the Vice-Presidential office, including being a Tanzanian citizen, at least 40 years old, and a member of a political party. He stressed that these qualifications apply even to appointed successors, not just those who 'contest' for the office. Interpreting Article 50(4) separately from Article 47 would lead to unreasonable outcomes, he warned.

tz.headline: President Samia Thanks Egyptian Envoy for Stronger Tanzania-Egypt Ties
tz.dek: President Samia Suluhu Hassan met with outgoing Egyptian Ambassador Sherif Ismail to acknowledge his contributions to bilateral cooperation.
paragraphs: President Samia Suluhu Hassan met with Egypt's Ambassador to Tanzania, Sherif Ismail, during his farewell visit to State House in Dar es Salaam. The President thanked Ambassador Ismail for his four-year tenure, during which he contributed to strengthening the long-standing and friendly relations between Tanzania and Egypt. She noted that cooperation has expanded across multiple sectors including trade, investment, education, health, agriculture, energy, tourism, and transport.

Discussions highlighted the importance of increasing trade and investment to maximize opportunities and benefit citizens of both nations. The leaders also addressed improving infrastructure and transport services to facilitate trade and create access to other African markets. In education, President Samia expressed gratitude for Egyptian scholarships and capacity-building programs offered to Tanzanians. Discussions also covered strengthening health sector cooperation through professional training, medical equipment access, and pharmaceutical production.

Both President Samia and Ambassador Ismail emphasized the importance of sustaining cooperation in these and other areas of mutual interest. This continued collaboration is seen as crucial for strengthening overall diplomatic and economic relations between Tanzania and Egypt. The meeting concluded with an acknowledgment of the progress made during the ambassador's term and a commitment to future engagement.

tz.headline: Tanzania, DR Congo Agree to Repatriate Refugees
tz.dek: The two nations and UNHCR will begin a voluntary repatriation process for Congolese refugees in Tanzania.
paragraphs: Tanzania and the Democratic Republic of Congo, in conjunction with the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR), have agreed to start a voluntary repatriation process for Congolese refugees residing in Tanzania. Deputy Minister of Home Affairs, Ayoub Mohammed Mahmoud, announced this decision at a Tripartite Commission Meeting in Lubumbashi. He stated that Tanzania will ensure the return is voluntary, safe, and dignified, without any coercion.

For those not yet ready to return, Tanzania will continue to provide asylum and services at the Nyarugusu Refugee Camp in Kigoma, utilizing available resources. The voluntary repatriation process will not impede Tanzania's ability to accept new asylum seekers fleeing insecurity in parts of the DRC. The Deputy Minister also urged DRC leaders to visit Nyarugusu Camp to engage directly with their citizens and address their needs.

The agreement aims to create an enabling environment for refugees willing to return to reunite with their families and contribute to their nation's development. The DRC leaders' visits are intended to build connection and hope, not to persuade refugees to return. Both nations committed to facilitating the return of those who wish to go back to their home country.

ma.headline: Moroccan-origin man arrested for Barcelona wildfire
ma.dek: Police detained a man after witnesses reported seeing him near the fire's origin with lighters, as investigators probe deliberate ignition.
paragraphs: A Moroccan-origin man is in custody following a wildfire in Barcelona’s Collserola mountain range that scorched over 54 hectares and led to the evacuation of 35 residents. Municipal police arrested the suspect after witnesses allegedly saw him setting fire to containers near Alta de Roquetes road. Investigators found several lighters in his possession and are examining them, along with a cigarette butt recovered near the suspected origin, for links to the man.

The fire, which began Tuesday afternoon and persisted through Wednesday, spread across more than 50 hectares of the Collserola mountain range, prompting authorities to evacuate nearby residents due to its proximity to populated areas. Catalan police are working to reconstruct the suspect’s movements and compare evidence from the fire's origin with items found on him. The investigation aims to determine if the fire was intentionally set and if the suspect bears criminal responsibility.

The suspect reportedly told officers he heard voices instructing him to start fires, a claim investigators are expected to consider. Authorities have not yet definitively linked the recovered evidence to the blaze. This incident occurs as Spain remains on high alert for wildfires during the summer months, with several regions experiencing fires near populated areas.

ug.headline: King Oyo's Fast Sparked Museveni's Weight Loss Remark
ug.dek: The Tooro King's 2014 protest fast over territory division drew a blunt response from President Museveni, highlighting enduring tensions.
paragraphs: In July 2014, Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV of Tooro Kingdom announced a six-day fast to protest the creation of new cultural institutions in Kasese and Bundibugyo, which he viewed as a division of his ancestral territory. The move followed the formal recognition of Obusinga Bwa Rwenzururu and Obudhingiya Bwa Bwamba, areas historically under Tooro. King Oyo's officials stated the fast would express displeasure over the lack of consultation and the delayed return of kingdom assets.

President Yoweri Museveni, who had served as one of King Oyo's guardians since 1995, publicly commented on the planned fast, remarking that it would help the king "shape up and be healthy." This statement provoked anger in Fort Portal, leading to demonstrations and arrests. Tooro Kingdom officials demanded an apology, asserting that the President's words undermined the monarchy.

The six-day fast concluded without the new institutions being dissolved, though demands for the return of kingdom assets persisted, eventually leading to a 2019 Memorandum of Understanding. Despite the public exchange, Museveni maintained his role as guardian to King Oyo. The 2014 fasting incident remains a notable moment of tension between the Tooro throne and the central government during the king's reign.

ug.headline: Stanbic Bank Funds Marathon for Maternal Health Services
ug.dek: The second annual Independence Marathon, themed "Save a Mother," will raise funds for maternal health at Mengo Hospital.
paragraphs: Stanbic Bank Uganda is sponsoring the upcoming Independence Marathon, an event aimed at reducing maternal mortality. The October 4 race, themed "Save a Mother," will direct its proceeds to enhancing maternal health services at Mengo Hospital. Diana Ondoga, manager for Corporate and Social Investment at Stanbic Bank Uganda, stated that the partnership highlights sport's capacity to unite communities for national causes. The marathon is expected to draw participants from various groups, including professional and amateur runners, corporate teams, and the general public.

The race will commence and conclude at Mandela National Stadium, utilizing the Northern Bypass for a professionally managed and timed course. Uganda's maternal mortality ratio has decreased to 207 deaths per 100,000 live births, according to the 2024 National Population and Housing Census, a significant drop from 336 deaths per 100,000 in 2016. This initiative seeks to further improve these statistics by strengthening healthcare services.

Health professionals and advocates are urging public support for the cause. Dr. Frank Kakuba of Mengo Hospital encouraged voluntary blood donations, a sentiment echoed by safe-motherhood advocate Daniel Lubwama Kigozi, also known as Navio. Both emphasized the critical need for blood donations to assist mothers experiencing severe bleeding during childbirth, a common cause of maternal mortality.

ug.headline: Attorney General Warns Against Expressway Contract Termination
ug.dek: Uganda risks costly international arbitration if the contract for the Kampala-Entebbe Expressway operator is terminated without following proper procedures, the Attorney General.
paragraphs: The Attorney General has cautioned against the immediate termination of the private operator's contract for the Kampala-Entebbe Expressway, warning that Uganda could face expensive international arbitration if contractual procedures are not followed. Deputy Attorney General Jackson Karugaba Kafuuzi presented this warning to Parliament as legislators reviewed recommendations from an inquiry into the expressway's management and toll collection.

Parliament's Committee on Physical Infrastructure called for the termination of French company EGIS Road Operation S.A.'s contract, which began on May 24, 2021, and is valued at Shs122.86 billion. The committee cited incomplete installations of traffic monitoring systems, inadequate lighting, and shortcomings in weigh-in-motion systems as justification for transferring operations to the Ministry of Works and Transport and toll collection to the Uganda Revenue Authority.

However, Kafuuzi advised the Ministry of Works and Transport to conduct a thorough assessment to determine if EGIS's alleged failures meet the contractual threshold for termination. He emphasized that the operator must first be formally notified of any breaches and given 14 days to rectify them, with liquidated damages and payment reductions applicable for delayed works before termination can be considered.
ug.body:

ug.headline: Court Clears Extradition of Ugandan Soldier to US for Drug Charges
ug.dek: A former UPDF soldier will face trial in the United States for cocaine trafficking, illegal firearms, and supporting a cartel.
paragraphs: Michael Katungi Mpeirwe, a former soldier in the Uganda People's Defence Force, has been committed to Luzira prison by the Buganda Road Chief Magistrates Court. This action awaits a decision from the Minister of Justice and Constitutional Affairs regarding his extradition to the United States. Katungi is wanted in the US to stand trial on charges including cocaine trafficking, illegal firearms possession, and providing material support to a Mexican drug cartel designated as a foreign terrorist organization.

Chief Magistrate Ritah Kidasa Neumbe dismissed all preliminary objections raised by Katungi, ruling that the Ugandan government met the legal threshold for committal under the Extradition Act. The US seeks Katungi for an alleged international drug-trafficking and weapons conspiracy, facing three counts in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia. These charges involve conspiring to distribute cocaine, possess firearms for drug trafficking, and provide support to the Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generación.

Katungi was initially brought before the court on June 29, 2026, following an arrest warrant requested by the US government. His legal team challenged the extradition process, citing procedural issues, the authority of officials, diplomatic immunity claims, and the admissibility of US evidence. The court, however, rejected these objections, paving the way for the extradition process to proceed.

ug.headline: Uganda Youth Face Jobless Future Despite Education Investments
ug.dek: Millions of young Ugandans struggle to find meaningful work due to skills mismatches and weak school-to-work transitions, despite significant national and international investment.
paragraphs: Uganda's large youth population, with nearly 78 percent under 30, presents a significant demographic dividend, yet economic participation remains constrained. Each year, approximately 700,000 young Ugandans enter the labor market, but only about 200,000 secure formal employment. Young women, refugees, and rural youth face the most substantial barriers to finding work.

Despite extensive investments in education, entrepreneurship, and digital skills development, these efforts alone are insufficient to unlock the country's demographic potential or foster inclusive growth. Experts suggest that developing skills must be coupled with creating environments that integrate new ideas with institutional knowledge and shared leadership.

The challenge lies not in a lack of aspiration among young people, who seek quality education and decent work, but in economies failing to connect generations and transform potential into productivity. This disconnect poses a growing economic risk for the nation.

zw.headline: World Bank removes Zimbabwe from Fragile States list
zw.dek: The country's removal from the World Bank's Fragile and Conflict-Affected Economies classification signals recognition of economic reforms.
paragraphs: Zimbabwe has been removed from the World Bank's Fragile and Conflict-Affected Economies classification, effective July 1, 2026. Finance Minister Mthuli Ncube stated this delisting validates the ongoing economic turnaround, governance, and institutional reforms under the government's Vision 2030 roadmap. The World Bank updated its framework in July 2026, splitting the old category into two metrics: the Public FCV List and the Institutional Fragility List. Zimbabwe's omission from both removes a significant sovereign risk label.

Ncube welcomed the move as international recognition of policy consistency and macroeconomic stability, adding that Treasury remains committed to boosting institutional resilience and inclusive growth. He expressed a goal to translate this renewed global confidence into tangible investments, jobs, and improved local livelihoods. Global investment bank Citigroup also praised the country's macroeconomic stabilization, noting that investors holding outdated perceptions risk missing opportunities in the ongoing recovery.

Citigroup reported that Zimbabwe is breaking decisively with its history of hyperinflation and currency instability. The bank highlighted that investors clinging to outdated perceptions of economic turbulence risk missing out on significant opportunities created by the ongoing recovery. Ncube projected the economy to register a conservative 5 percent growth this year, following an 8 percent expansion in 2025.

zw.headline: Chiwenga's Wife Earns Doctorate Degree
zw.dek: Miniyothabo Chiwenga received a Doctor of Business Leadership degree from Midlands State University among 7,888 graduates.
paragraphs: Midlands State University (MSU) conferred degrees on seven thousand eight hundred and eighty-eight graduands, including Vice President Chiwenga’s wife, Miniyothabo, who earned a Doctor of Business Leadership degree. The 27th graduation ceremony, held at the Emmerson Dambudzo Mnangagwa Law School, focused on the theme “Knowledge, Innovation, and Enterprise: Building a Self-Sufficient Zimbabwe.” Female students comprised fifty-five percent of the graduating cohort, continuing a trend of women outnumbering men.

MSU Vice Chancellor Professor Victor Muzvidziwa stated the ceremony held national significance, celebrating sacrifice and intellectual labour aligned with the National Development Strategy 2 and Vision 2030. He noted that nineteen graduands received Doctor of Philosophy or Doctor of Business Leadership degrees, while thirty-nine percent completed degrees in critical skills disciplines like science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. The university also celebrated its first graduates in Biomedical Sciences and specialized engineering fields.

Colonel Miniyothabo Francisca Baloyi-Chiwenga’s doctoral research explored balancing defence expenditure with civilian priorities. After receiving her degree, she emphasized the importance of hard work and perseverance for young Zimbabweans, particularly the girl child, stating that success requires dedication and has no shortcuts. Zimpapers Group Digital Services Executive Elias Mambo was also among the graduates, earning a Master of Commerce Degree in Strategy and Innovation.

zw.headline: Government Denies Millers Shut Down Over Maize Shortage
zw.dek: The Ministry of Agriculture has rejected claims that Blue Ribbon Industries and 23 other millers have ceased operations due to a lack of maize.
paragraphs: The Zimbabwean government has refuted reports that major milling companies, including Blue Ribbon Industries and 23 others in Bulawayo, have shut down operations because of a maize shortage. The Ministry of Agriculture stated that it obtained information directly from the companies which contradicts the claims. Officials accused "elitist interests" of fabricating a national grain crisis to push for increased imports.

These denials follow a circular attributed to the Grain Millers Association of Zimbabwe (GMAZ) Southern Region chairperson, Major (Rtd) David Moyo, which alleged a significant decline in local maize supplies. Moyo's circular claimed this had affected millers' ability to maintain production and build reserves, leading to the reported closures in Bulawayo. The government, however, maintains that Zimbabwe has produced more maize, with output rising 17.1% from 2.29 million tonnes in 2025 to 2.69 million tonnes in 2026.

The Ministry acknowledged localized supply and quality issues, such as insect infestation in some grain stocks, but insisted these should not be amplified into a national shortage. This dispute occurs amidst an ongoing disagreement over government policies, specifically the grain import levy framework introduced under Statutory Instrument 87 of 2025, which millers oppose due to increased costs. The government asserts these levies protect local farmers and promote domestic production.

zw.headline: Tshuma murder case postponed to September 8-10
zw.dek: Johannesburg court hears extradition case of British Zimbabwean accused of killing his wife and two daughters in the UK.
paragraphs: The murder and extradition case against Ndodana Tshuma has been postponed by the Johannesburg Magistrate’s Court to September 8 and 10. Tshuma, 45, is accused of killing his wife, Nothabo Zandile Tshuma, and their two daughters, Natalie and Nala, in Bedford, UK, where the family resided.

Tshuma, a British citizen of Zimbabwean heritage, was apprehended in Johannesburg after being seen leaving Heathrow Airport. He appeared briefly in court and abandoned a bail application related to possession of an illegal firearm. The court is expected to continue proceedings on the specified dates.

The case involves allegations of triple murder in the United Kingdom, with Tshuma facing extradition. His brief court appearance focused on the immediate charges in South Africa while the broader extradition process is underway. Further details are anticipated during the upcoming court dates.

cv.headline: Dutch court sentences Rwandan man to life for 1994 genocide
cv.dek: A 66-year-old man was convicted of genocide, pillaging, and destruction of property during Rwanda's 1994 violence.
paragraphs: A Dutch court has sentenced a 66-year-old Rwandan man to life imprisonment for his role in the 1994 genocide. The Hague District Court found him guilty of genocide, pillaging, and destruction of homes during the wave of violence. The judge stated the offenses deeply shocked society and constituted a considerable violation of the legal order in Rwanda and worldwide.

The prosecution accused the man of personally throwing a grenade into a stadium filled with men, women, and children in Mbazi, southern Rwanda, where approximately three thousand people seeking refuge were massacred. He denied the charges, claiming he was also a victim of violence and that family members were killed. The suspect, who has held Dutch nationality since 1998, cannot be extradited to Rwanda.

Dutch investigators have been examining the case since 2020, interviewing dozens of witnesses, including in Rwanda. European courts have used the principle of universal jurisdiction to try individuals involved in the Rwandan genocide, allowing prosecution for severe crimes committed abroad. The United Nations reports that over eight hundred thousand people, primarily from the Tutsi minority, were killed in Rwanda during the spring of 1994.

cv.headline: Cape Verde Basketball Team Loses to Guinea-Conakry
cv.dek: The Blue Sharks fell to a 61-81 defeat against Guinea-Conakry in their 2027 World Cup qualifying match.
paragraphs: Cape Verde's national basketball team, the Blue Sharks, suffered a significant loss to Guinea-Conakry with a final score of 61-81. The match, part of the African qualifiers for the 2027 World Cup in Qatar, saw Cape Verde lose across all four quarters: 16-23, 18-23, 16-17, and 11-18. This defeat follows an earlier loss to Tunisia in the same qualifying window.

According to the Cape Verdean Basketball Federation (FCBB), the team's performance was outmatched by the hosts. This game marked the beginning of their qualification campaign. The team is scheduled for another match on Sunday, the thirtieth, at two o'clock in the afternoon Cape Verde time, also in Tunis, concluding this qualification window.

The Blue Sharks are competing in Group E of the African qualification phase for the upcoming World Cup. Their next fixture is against Tunisia, a rematch of their opening game where they narrowly lost 56-60. The team's current standing in the group is not detailed, but these two consecutive losses present a challenging start to their qualification journey.

cv.headline: Young People Leave Rural Cape Verde for Opportunities
cv.dek: Internal migration data shows a significant outflow of youth from rural areas, impacting production and local economies.
paragraphs: Rural areas of Cape Verde are experiencing a decline in population, particularly among young people, leading to reduced production capacity and fewer opportunities for renewal. This internal migration is driven by a lack of jobs, inadequate training, and limited prospects for personal fulfillment in these communities. The trend, while part of Cape Verde's history of migration, becomes problematic when leaving is a necessity rather than a choice.

Data from the 2021 Census reveals a clear pattern of internal population movement. Coastal areas like Praia, Sal, and São Vicente recorded positive internal migration balances, gaining thousands of residents. Conversely, municipalities such as Ribeira Grande de Santo Antão, Santa Catarina, São Miguel, and Porto Novo showed negative balances, indicating a loss of inhabitants. This uneven distribution highlights disparities in opportunities across the nation.

The depopulation of rural zones has consequences beyond demographics, affecting agricultural labor, local businesses, and the transmission of knowledge. As young people depart, land may go unworked, diminishing food production potential and economic prospects. Revitalizing these areas requires modernization, improved water management, technology adoption, and better integration with tourism and consumer markets to create viable life projects.

cv.headline: Praia Firefighters Seek Modern Equipment Amidst Urban Growth
cv.dek: The Praia Fire Department, celebrating 48 years, faces challenges from the expanding city and calls for updated facilities and specialized gear.
paragraphs: The Praia Fire Department is requesting improved resources to address the demands of the city's rapid urban expansion. Commander Carlos Teixeira stated that the growing city and population require new conditions and more modern, adequate facilities to meet the needs of residents. He noted that the current station is old and no longer fully meets the requirements of an expanding city, emphasizing the need for modern infrastructure to keep pace with urban development.

Teixeira also highlighted the increasing number of multi-story buildings as a significant challenge, requiring specialized equipment for high-rise firefighting. He welcomed the initiative by the Praia Municipal Assembly President to provide an aerial ladder truck in partnership with the government, which will enhance intervention capabilities in tall buildings. The department handles a substantial number of daily incidents, with medical emergencies being prominent, averaging ten to fifteen ambulance calls daily.

The commander stressed that effective response relies on both available resources and personnel preparedness, with better material and infrastructural conditions contributing to more efficient interventions. He praised the dedication of the firefighters, describing their work as invaluable for public protection and assistance. Teixeira expressed his motivation to continue working towards better conditions for the firefighters to serve the population of Praia more effectively.

td.headline: New Governor Installed in Chad's Salamat Province
td.dek: Ahmat Choua Rozi officially assumed leadership of the Salamat province on Friday, August 28, 2026, following a government decree.
paragraphs: Ahmat Choua Rozi was officially installed as the new Governor of Salamat province on Friday, August 28, 2026, in Am-Timan. The ceremony was presided over by Limane Mahamat, the Vice-Prime Minister for Territorial Administration and Decentralization. The installation follows decree n° 2122 issued on August 3, 2026. The outgoing governor, General Ismat Issakha Acheikh, expressed pride in his tenure, stating that his achievements in the province speak for themselves and were made possible through the collaboration of all provincial stakeholders.

Vice-Prime Minister Limane Mahamat reminded the new Governor of his responsibilities, emphasizing his role as the dignified face of the state, a guarantor of civil peace, social cohesion, and public tranquility. He stressed the shared responsibility to consolidate security in Salamat and ensure its progress benefits all its inhabitants. The Minister instructed Rozi to proactively address and neutralize potential sources of tension before they escalate.

The newly installed Governor, Ahmat Choua Rozi, conveyed his gratitude to President Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno for the trust placed in him. Rozi pledged to carry out his duties with impartiality, rigor, humility, and a constant spirit of dialogue, in accordance with the Republic's laws. The ceremony in Am-Timan was attended by a large, engaged crowd.

td.headline: Syria Reconnects to Global Card Payments After 15 Years
td.dek: Mastercard and QNB Group processed the first international card transaction in Syria, marking a significant step in modernizing the country's payment systems.
paragraphs: Mastercard and QNB Group have successfully completed the first international card transaction in Syria in over 15 years. This event signifies a major advancement in the nation's payment infrastructure, reconnecting its system to the global Mastercard network. QNB Syria processed the transaction using an internationally issued Mastercard on a local point-of-sale terminal with an eligible merchant.

This milestone transaction lays the groundwork for accepting international payments within Syria, aiming to integrate consumers, businesses, and financial institutions into the global digital economy. The Governor of the Central Bank of Syria, S.E. Mohammed Safwat Raslan, stated that this achievement demonstrates the value of public-private collaboration in enabling secure international payment acceptance and fostering sustainable economic development.

Yousef Mahmoud Al-Neama of QNB Group highlighted that providing merchants with international payment capabilities offers customers more choices and convenience, supporting a transition to a more modern and secure digital payment ecosystem. Adam Jones of Mastercard added that this is a crucial step towards broader and more secure digital payment acceptance across the market, fostering a more connected and inclusive payment environment.

td.headline: ONASER Educates Road Users on Traffic Law Compliance
td.dek: The National Road Safety Office conducted a campaign across N'Djamena intersections to remind drivers and pedestrians of traffic regulations.
paragraphs: The National Road Safety Office (ONASER) deployed teams to several intersections in N'Djamena's Project for the Improvement of the Douala-N'Djamena Road Corridor (PCDN) area on Friday. The campaign aimed to inform road users about the importance of strictly adhering to traffic laws, including obeying road signs, speed limits, and instructions related to ongoing construction work.

ONASER urged all users to exercise caution, vigilance, and civic responsibility, especially near construction zones. The goal is to reduce accident risks and ensure the safety of workers, residents, and all road users. Drivers of 'clandos,' motorcyclists, motorists, and pedestrians were targeted in the awareness drive.

Those who participated in the sensitization expressed satisfaction with the initiative and pledged to adopt responsible driving habits. ONASER reiterated that everyone shares responsibility on the road and that respecting rules is crucial for saving lives. The campaign focused on promoting safer road practices within the city.

td.headline: Armed men intrude on journalist's home claiming security search
td.dek: Four masked men, identifying as national security agents, entered a journalist's home without a warrant, later admitting they had the wrong address.
paragraphs: Journalist Hynda Ahmet Chérif reported an armed intrusion at her home on Friday, August 28, 2026. Four masked men, carrying pistols and knives, entered her residence during the day while several occupants were at the mosque for prayer. The men claimed to be from the National Security Agency and stated they were conducting a search based on a tip.

When Chérif repeatedly asked for a warrant, the armed men refused, asserting they needed no official documentation. The situation shifted when a household employee questioned if they were at the correct home. After confirming Chérif's identity, one man made a phone call and the group departed on motorcycles, with one apologizing for the mistake and claiming they had the wrong house.

This incident has raised significant concerns about citizen safety and the sanctity of private residences. The journalist is questioning the true identity of the intruders, uncertain if they were genuine state agents or criminals impersonating officials. The event highlights anxieties regarding state authority and potential misuse of power.

td.headline: Chadian and CAR Officials Discuss Border Conflicts
td.dek: Cross-border prefects from Chad and the Central African Republic met to address community disputes and explore strategic infrastructure corridors.
paragraphs: Officials from Chad's Logone Oriental region and the Central African Republic's Yadé province convened in Mbaïbokoum, southern Chad, for a two-day conference. Supported by Concordis International, the meeting aimed to enhance participants' skills in managing recurring border conflicts and to analyze the potential for creating corridors with strategic infrastructure.

The conference, themed 'Prevention and Management of Community Conflicts Related to Transhumance at the CAR-Chad Borders,' served as a platform for dialogue and information sharing. It focused on community disputes largely stemming from the transhumance of herders from West and Central Africa and Cameroon seeking pastureland, with the goal of establishing leadership and strategies to address these issues.

Prefect Idriss Souleymane Bouyemé of the Monts de Lam department highlighted that border areas face numerous security challenges, including agro-pastoral conflicts, land disputes, cross-border crime, and uncontrolled movements of people and livestock, all of which can undermine social cohesion.

dj.headline: Djibouti seeks solar expansion support from International Solar Alliance
dj.dek: Djibouti's energy minister met with the ISA director general to discuss rural electrification and solar infrastructure development.
paragraphs: Djibouti's Minister of Energy, Dr. Djama Mohamed Hassan, met with the Director General of the International Solar Alliance (ISA), Ashish Khanna, to advance solar energy deployment. The discussions focused on enhancing the partnership between Djibouti and the ISA, with specific attention to training, rural electrification, and the development of solar infrastructure. Djibouti requested ISA support for deploying solar mini-grids in twenty priority areas as part of its national rural electrification strategy.

The meeting also addressed the establishment of a regional STAR-C center in Djibouti, intended to serve as an expertise and training hub. This center aims to standardize photovoltaic equipment, strengthen quality standards, and develop regulatory frameworks to encourage solar investments. The initiative is expected to improve the oversight of photovoltaic installations' compliance and durability within the country.

ISA Director General Ashish Khanna highlighted the Alliance's initiatives for Africa, including a guarantee fund increased from seventy-one million euros to two hundred million euros to stimulate private investment in decentralized energy production. Khanna affirmed the ISA's continued support for realizing solar projects in Djibouti, commending the government's ambitious vision for sustainable development.

dj.headline: Djibouti Red Cross disburses funds to storm victims
dj.dek: The Djibouti Red Cross mobilized thirteen million, four hundred forty thousand Djiboutian francs to aid families in Mouloud whose roofs were damaged by high winds.
paragraphs: The Djibouti Red Cross has provided financial assistance totaling thirteen million, four hundred forty thousand Djiboutian francs to households in Mouloud affected by severe winds. Each family received eighty thousand Djiboutian francs to help with roof repairs or rehabilitation. This initiative is part of a multisectoral response to the violent winds in Mouloud, implemented with support from the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

The distribution followed field assessments by Red Cross teams and volunteers, who identified homes with destroyed or severely damaged roofs. Vulnerable families, including those headed by women, large families, the elderly, people with disabilities, and those with limited economic resources, received particular attention. The process involved coordination with local authorities and community structures.

The ceremony was attended by various officials, including the Secretary General of the Djibouti Red Cross, Amina Houssein Farah, and the deputy prefect of the Dikhil region, Idriss Houssein Abass. This financial transfer represents the culmination of efforts to support affected residents in rebuilding their homes and restoring their living conditions after the storm damage.

sz.headline: Eswatini Trade Fair and Rally Draw International and Local Talent
sz.dek: The Eswatini International Trade Fair and Swazi Rally are set to host a diverse range of performers and participants, attracting both regional stars and dedicated enthusiasts.
paragraphs: The Eswatini International Trade Fair will open with performances by South African artists Simmy and Mduduzi Ncube, blending Afro-Soul with folk and acoustic narratives. Local hip hop and contemporary Swati artists, including Young Zesh, Sancheziey, Mco Jamrock, and DJ Bandora, will also showcase indigenous lyrical flows and modern street culture. The event continues with a Gospel Sunday featuring South African headliner Jumbo alongside Eswatini's Phathwakahle, Ndawonye Christ Worshippers, and Shongwe and Khuphuka Saved Group.

Further entertainment includes a pop set by South African duo Q Twins and DJ Tira, complemented by Eswatini's saxophonist ZwiLe, who will introduce jazz-influenced textures. This cultural showcase aligns with national Umhlanga holiday celebrations. Separately, the 33rd edition of the Swazi Rally, an annual bikers' event established in 1993, will take place at Riders Ranch in Sidvokodvo. Organizers have expanded camping facilities due to increasing attendance.

The Swazi Rally, founded by Carlos Paiva and his wife Sonia, has a long-standing tradition, with some attendees participating since its inception. The event is described as the ultimate biker experience in Southern Africa, featuring roaring engines and nights under the stars. The rally's continuous development is attributed to the ownership of the site, offering picturesque scenery along its winding roads.

sz.headline: Green Chert Mine Halts Operations, Leaving Workers Unemployed
sz.dek: The mine's sudden closure has left between 80 and 100 workers jobless and cast doubt on community development projects.
paragraphs: Green Chert Mine, a project once heralded for its potential to create jobs and stimulate economic growth in northern Hhohho, has ceased operations. The mine's premises in Nkomazi were found deserted, with heavy machinery stationary since July 23, the day workers were informed of the halt. Former employees reported being verbally told operations were suspended 'until further notice,' a surprise announcement that left various categories of workers, from blasters to drivers, without income.

The mine's closure raises concerns about the future of promised community development initiatives, including two mini-shops and a spaza shop, as well as planned housing for displaced residents. These projects had generated optimism for long-term economic transformation in the traditionally rural area, with expectations of increased economic activity and improved infrastructure.

The halt affects workers across different roles, including stone parkers, sorters, blasters, drivers, and boilermakers, at both the Nkomazi headquarters and the extraction site near kaNdeva. The mine's development had previously attracted significant investment, with millions of Emalangeni reportedly invested, fueling hopes for a more urbanized community and enhanced livelihoods.

sz.dek: Mbali Dlamini aims to become the first Eswatini Cricket Association coach to achieve ICC Level 2 certification at a program in Tanzania.
paragraphs: Eswatini national women's cricket captain Mbali Dlamini is attending the ICC Future Leadership Programme for Female Coaches in Tanzania from August 29 to September 6. Dlamini, who has captained the national team since 2020, was selected for the program based on her progress through the ICC coaching development pathway. The initiative offers aspiring female coaches access to international expertise and mentorship, aiming to strengthen their coaching and leadership skills in an international setting.

The program presents an opportunity for Dlamini to potentially earn the ICC Level 2 Coaching Certificate, a qualification that would make her the first coach, male or female, in Eswatini Cricket Association history to achieve it. This milestone is significant for the country's efforts to grow its cricket infrastructure and develop a more robust pipeline of coaches, particularly in the women's game. The knowledge gained is expected to benefit players and future coaches back home.

Dlamini's participation is supported by the Eswatini Sport and Recreation Council and the Eswatini Olympics and Commonwealth Games Association. Her journey represents a significant step for Eswatini within an international coaching development program focused on the future of women's cricket. The immediate goal is for Dlamini to maximize her learning experience in Tanzania, which could mark the beginning of a new era for women's coaching in Eswatini.

sz.headline: Pam Golding Properties Relaunches in Eswatini
sz.dek: The international real estate brand marks a new chapter in the Kingdom with trusted local leadership and a commitment to personalized client experiences.
paragraphs: Pam Golding Properties has relaunched in Eswatini, establishing a new chapter built on heritage and continuity. The company, founded in South Africa in 1976, has evolved into a respected real estate brand with an international presence. This relaunch signifies confidence in Eswatini's property market potential and a commitment to partnering with experienced local professionals who align with the brand's values.

The relaunch is led by Musawenkosi C. Nhleko, principal and franchise holder of Pam Golding Properties Eswatini, along with his team of specialist real estate professionals. Nhleko and his wife, Nomcebo Nhleko, attended the 2026 GoldClub Gala Awards in Johannesburg, celebrating the company's 50th anniversary and its achievements.

Pam Golding Properties first entered Eswatini in 2003, opening an office in Ezulwini. The brand's return aims to build on its legacy in the Kingdom by combining deep local knowledge with the strength of its regional and international network. The company's ethos emphasizes trusted relationships, local expertise, market insight, and a dedication to delivering personalized client experiences.

sz.headline: Thousands of Maidens Complete Four-Day Umhlanga Reed March
sz.dek: Older Imbali, led by Princess Sakhizwe, concluded their return journey from Mpisi Farm after a physically demanding reed-cutting exercise.
paragraphs: Thousands of older Imbali yesterday began their return journey from Mpisi Farm, marking the fourth day of the Umhlanga ceremony. Led by Imbali Regiment Leader Princess Sakhizwe, the maidens marched towards Mafutseni, arriving at the police station after covering 5.9 kilometres. The procession was filled with singing and dancing, showcasing the endurance and energy of the participants who had gathered from across the kingdom.

The annual national ceremony began on Tuesday with the arrival and registration of thousands of maidens at Ludzidzini. The second day saw the maidens commissioned for the reed-cutting exercise, with King Mswati III directing older Imbali to Mpisi Farm and younger ones to Masundvwini. The third day was the most physically demanding, as older Imbali travelled to Mpisi Farm for the reed-cutting, officially opened by Princess Sakhizwe.

Participants from various chiefdoms, including contingents from the Royal Eswatini Police Service, Eswatini Defence Force, and Eswatini National Fire, Rescue and Emergency Services, joined the reed-cutting. Maidens sang and danced as they gathered reeds, assisted by Emazinyane and tindvuna, preparing them for the return journey to the royal residence.

ga.headline: President Inaugurates New Hospital in Booué
ga.dek: The new departmental hospital in Booué, inaugurated by President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, aims to improve healthcare access for local populations.
paragraphs: President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema officially opened the Booué Departmental Hospital Center on Friday, an event attended by Health Minister Pr Elsa Nkana Joséphine Ayo épouse Bivigou. This new facility, spanning 850 square meters, is equipped with 24 beds and offers services in surgery, maternity, and general medicine, alongside an operating room, laboratory, and medical consultations. The establishment of this hospital represents a significant investment of nearly one and a half billion FCFA.

The project was funded through SETRAG's corporate social responsibility policy, with the explicit goal of enhancing health infrastructure in this region of Gabon. Local health workers and residents have expressed their satisfaction with the new center, which is expected to reduce the need for patients to travel to other towns for medical care. The hospital is now better equipped to address various medical needs within Booué and its surrounding areas.

This development provides the inhabitants of Booué with improved medical facilities, ensuring more immediate and accessible healthcare. The presence of essential services within the community is anticipated to alleviate pressure on existing, more distant healthcare providers and improve overall public health outcomes.

ga.headline: Bosch Capital Demands $330 Million Debt Payment from Gabon
ga.dek: The South African fund threatens to damage Gabon's financial reputation if the debt from military equipment purchases is not settled by September 3.
paragraphs: Bosch Capital, a South African fund that acquired rights to a debt from Paramount Group, is demanding over $300 million from Gabon. The fund has set a September 3 deadline for Libreville to pay. In a letter dated August 24, Bosch Capital warned of actions that could negatively impact Gabon's financial standing. This debt originates from maintenance and support services for military equipment, stemming from a 2014 contract, and has accumulated to approximately $330 million.

The fund, represented by Seven Pillars Law, is attempting to resolve a financial dispute by pressuring the Gabonese state. Bosch Capital has indicated it may inform international financial system actors if its demand is not met. This threat extends beyond legal action, potentially affecting Gabon's sovereign risk perception among rating agencies, banks, and international investors.

The debt is linked to past military equipment transactions. In 2006-2007, Gabon acquired Mirage F1AZ aircraft from Paramount Group and Aerosud, which were previously part of the South African Air Force. Bosch Capital's claim is rooted in a 2014 contract for maintenance and support of military equipment, with the current amount reflecting accumulated sums and litigation developments.

ga.headline: TotalEnergies EP Gabon Profit Plummets 87% Despite Favorable Oil Market
ga.dek: The company's net profit fell to six million dollars in the second quarter of 2026, impacted by stock position changes and increased operating costs.
paragraphs: TotalEnergies EP Gabon reported an 87% drop in net profit for the second quarter of 2026, reaching six million dollars, despite a favorable oil market. The company's revenue increased by thirteen percent to one hundred eleven million dollars, driven by rising crude prices. The average Brent crude price rose twenty-eight percent to one hundred three point eight dollars per barrel during this period, while TotalEnergies EP Gabon's commercialized crude averaged one hundred point two dollars per barrel, up seven percent.

The significant profit decline was primarily attributed to a negative stock position variation of sixty-nine million dollars. Additionally, higher operating expenses and non-operational financial charges reduced earnings by six million dollars. These impacts were partially offset by revenue growth, a twenty-one million dollar decrease in tax charges, and a five million dollar reduction in depreciation.

For the first half of 2026, TotalEnergies EP Gabon maintained a solid net profit of fifty-one million dollars. Revenue for the semester was two hundred nine million dollars, a four percent decrease year-on-year, mainly due to a reduced export schedule. Crude oil production saw a slight increase to fifteen point six thousand barrels per day in the first half.

ga.headline: Gabon hires 248 volunteer teachers into public service
ga.dek: Two hundred forty-eight teachers who previously volunteered in Ogooué-Ivindo province have been officially integrated into the civil service.
paragraphs: The formal integration of 248 teachers into Gabon's public service was marked by a ceremony in Makokou on Friday, August 28, 2026. These educators had been volunteering in public schools in the Ogooué-Ivindo province for years, often under precarious administrative conditions. The event, attended by Minister of State for National Education and Civic Instruction, Camélia Ntoutoume Leclercq, involved the distribution of certificates and initial payment vouchers, recognizing their commitment, training, and qualifications.

This regularization process acknowledges the teachers' dedication and the essential role they played in the education system despite administrative uncertainties. Their integration into the civil service signifies a tangible fulfillment of promises, transitioning them from volunteer status to fully recognized and salaried public employees. Minister Ntoutoume Leclercq emphasized the professional recognition this change represents, stating they are no longer volunteers but certified educators.

The provincial director of education for Ogooué-Ivindo, Jean Lin Essié Effé, expressed gratitude to the government for its efforts in the education sector, specifically highlighting the regularization of these former volunteers. Beneficiaries shared their long-awaited satisfaction, noting that this recognition of their years of work provides renewed motivation to serve Gabonese schools with commitment and responsibility. The state aims to strengthen its teaching staff with these qualified and integrated professionals.

ga.headline: Children Learn Galoa Language to Preserve Cultural Heritage
ga.dek: An interactive workshop in Ntyatanga village aims to teach young people the ancestral Galoa language, fostering cultural memory and identity.
paragraphs: In Ntyatanga village, Moyen-Ogooué province, children recently participated in a Galoa language learning workshop. The initiative uses participatory methods to encourage the transmission of this ancestral tongue, aiming to empower youth as guardians of cultural heritage. The workshop focused on oral and written practice in a relaxed environment, emphasizing progress through shared correction and confidence-building.

Led by Francis Akita, Victor Vériany, and Arthur Lamie Akendengue, the workshop covered basic communication, sentence structure, pronouns, vocabulary, numbers, and body parts. Interactive methods like role-playing, debates, and pronunciation exercises were employed to engage children and instill a desire to speak, understand, and write Galoa. The organizers believe that preserving traditional languages is crucial for maintaining collective memory, values, and knowledge.

The event highlighted the ongoing challenge of ensuring the Galoa language remains actively used within families and by younger generations. Potential future actions include more frequent workshops, intergenerational gatherings, and the creation of educational materials to support the language's continuity. The initiative underscores that a language's survival depends on its active use, teaching, and valorization by those who will carry it forward.

gm.headline: Gambia flags 74 stolen vehicles after 13,000 Interpol checks
gm.dek: Joint security forces used Interpol databases to screen travelers and vehicles at key entry points around Banjul.
paragraphs: Gambian security forces intercepted 74 stolen vehicles during a two-week border operation near Banjul, following over 13,000 checks against Interpol databases. The operation involved immigration, police, customs, and prison officers, along with The Gambia’s Interpol National Central Bureau. Using mobile devices connected to Interpol systems, teams screened individuals and vehicles for links to terrorism, drug trafficking, and human trafficking.

The checks resulted in 74 stolen vehicles being flagged, highlighting the extent of cross-border vehicle theft networks in the region. This operation, part of Project Identity, provided training and equipment for officers to access Interpol databases in real time. Interpol stated that the coordinated checks aimed to intercept wanted individuals and illicit goods at key locations around Banjul.

Vehicle theft and transnational crime have historically exploited West Africa's borders, with stolen cars often trafficked and sold with forged documents. The recent operation signifies a shift towards intelligence-led screening backed by global databases, a critical capability for The Gambia in tackling organized crime at its busy entry points.
