rw.headline: Rwanda Central Bank Hikes Rate to 8.75% as Inflation Reaches 14.5%
rw.dek: The National Bank of Rwanda tightened monetary policy for the second quarter, raising its benchmark interest rate by 50 basis points to combat accelerating inflation.
paragraphs: KIGALI – Rwanda’s central bank has increased its benchmark interest rate by 50 basis points to 8.75%, signaling a further tightening of monetary policy. The decision, announced by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) on August 26, comes as inflation surged to 14.5% in July, significantly exceeding the bank’s target range of 2%-8%. This move extends the monetary tightening cycle that commenced in late 2025.

Headline inflation has climbed from 9.1% in the first quarter of 2026 to 13.2% in the second quarter, culminating in the 14.5% figure for July. The National Bank of Rwanda (BNR) now projects inflation to average 13.1% for 2026, a slight downward revision from the previous forecast of 13.9%. The MPC attributed the persistent inflation to rising costs in core goods, fresh food, and energy, with energy inflation alone surging to 45.7%.

The BNR anticipates inflation will remain above the target range throughout 2026, with a gradual return expected in the latter half of 2027, forecasting 7.9% for that year. Potential risks include the El Niño climate pattern affecting food prices and ongoing Middle East tensions impacting global commodity costs. Despite these pressures, Rwanda’s economy demonstrated strong growth, expanding by 10% year-on-year in the first quarter of 2026.

rw.headline: Rwanda Selects Top Coffees for October Auction
rw.dek: Twenty-five award-winning coffees will be offered to international buyers in an online auction on October 21, aiming to boost export value.
paragraphs: Rwanda has chosen 25 of its finest coffees for an international auction scheduled for October 21. This initiative, following the Best of Rwanda National Specialty Coffee Competition, aims to increase the value of the country's coffee exports and solidify its standing in the global specialty market. The winning lots were recognized on August 27 in Kigali after being selected from 320 samples submitted by cooperatives and processing companies nationwide.

The competition, organized by the National Agricultural Export Development Board (NAEB), identifies exceptional coffees and connects producers with specialty market buyers, where higher prices can be achieved. K-Organics coffee from Huye District won the Anaerobic Natural category, while Great Coffee Farmers Ltd’s Cyeza Coffee Washing Station in Muhanga District secured first place in the Fully Washed category. Last year, K-Organics' winning coffee sold for $88 per kilogram, an increase from previous years.

NAEB Director General Claude Bizimana stated the competition's goal is to promote Rwandan coffee internationally, expand markets, and increase export earnings. Agriculture Minister Telesphore Ndabamenye emphasized coffee's economic importance and called for improved quality and value across the coffee chain. The 25 selected coffees will be available through an online auction, offering producers a chance to translate quality recognition into greater financial returns.

rw.headline: RSSB Acquires Full Control of Inyange and Ruliba Clays
rw.dek: The Rwanda Social Security Board now owns 100% of two companies after purchasing remaining shares from Crystal Ventures Limited.
paragraphs: The Rwanda Social Security Board (RSSB) has acquired the remaining shares in Inyange Industries and Ruliba Clays from Crystal Ventures Limited (CVL), securing full ownership of both companies. This transaction grants RSSB complete control over the future expansion plans for these two entities. The deal was announced on Thursday, August 27, marking the end of a long-standing arrangement.

While RSSB has a history of successful investments, the specifics of this acquisition remain undisclosed, raising questions about accountability. Information regarding the purchase price for each company, their independent valuations, profitability, liabilities, and expected returns for pensioners has not been provided by RSSB officials despite repeated requests. This lack of transparency is particularly notable given CVL's association with the ruling RPF.

RSSB officials have been criticized for their response to inquiries, with their perceived arrogance and disrespect fostering an impression of a family-run business rather than a statutory institution. While the transaction itself is not inherently improper and may prove to be a sound investment, the close relationship between the buyer and seller necessitates a higher standard of transparency and clear disclosure of financial details and due diligence processes.

rw.headline: Rwanda C-Section Rate Doubles to 24%, Prompting Health Debate
rw.dek: The nation's surgical birth rate has more than doubled since 2000, reaching 24% and sparking questions about medical necessity versus other contributing factors.
paragraphs: Rwanda's Caesarean section rate has climbed to 24%, according to the latest Rwanda Demographic and Health Survey (RDHS7). This significant increase, more than double the World Health Organization's 10% benchmark for population-level impact, is prompting renewed debate about the drivers behind the growing number of surgical births.

The current rate represents a substantial rise from 15.6% in 2019-20 and a dramatic jump from 2.2% in 2000. While C-sections can be life-saving when medically necessary, experts question whether the current trend is solely driven by complications or influenced by other factors, such as higher rates in private facilities which previously stood at 60.6% compared to 15.4% in public ones.

This rise in surgical births occurs alongside progress in reducing maternal deaths, with the ratio declining from 203 per 100,000 live births in 2020 to 149 in 2025. However, health experts emphasize that the priority is ensuring C-sections are performed when medically required, while avoiding unnecessary procedures, making understanding the root causes of the increase critical for public health.

st.headline: Constitutional Court President Considers Resignation After Elections
st.dek: Artur Vera Cruz, President of the Constitutional Court, is contemplating stepping down post-September 27 elections, citing his status as a civil servant.
paragraphs: Artur Vera Cruz, President of the Constitutional Court of São Tomé and Príncipe, is considering leaving his post after the legislative, municipal, and regional elections scheduled for September 27. Vera Cruz stated that as an employee of the Court of Accounts, he had requested a six-month leave and is now reflecting on his return to his original position, distancing his decision from internal institutional crises or disputes with the Supreme Court of Justice.

The potential departure comes amid internal disagreements with the court's vice-president and a public conflict with the Supreme Court of Justice. The latter rejected a Constitutional Court ruling concerning the release of a Chilean citizen detained on Interpol's request for alleged tax crimes. Vera Cruz clarified that the court did not usurp authority but recommended alternative measures to detention within 24 hours, such as house arrest or regular court appearances.

Vera Cruz made these remarks following a draw by the Constitutional Court to determine the order of seven political parties on the legislative election ballot. The MCI/PS-PUN coalition will lead the ballot, followed by Nossa Terra, Basta, MLSTP, PCD, MDFM, and ADI. The Constitutional Court has not yet validated the final list of parties for the September 27 elections.

st.headline: IMF, World Bank policies drive debt system in African nations
st.dek: Austerity measures tied to debt servicing are creating common economic and social challenges across geographically diverse African countries.
paragraphs: African nations are increasingly burdened by their public debt, a situation exacerbated by policies promoted by the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. These institutions advocate for austerity measures as a means to service national debts, a strategy that directly impacts public budgets. This approach often necessitates maintaining a high primary surplus, which in turn leads to persistent cuts in social spending and a reduction in investments allocated to essential public services.

This common economic predicament, driven by what is termed the 'debt system,' forces countries to prioritize debt repayment over social welfare and development. The consequence is a growing commitment of public funds towards debt servicing, leaving fewer resources available for critical sectors such as education, healthcare, and infrastructure development. This pattern is observed across many nations, regardless of their specific geographical or cultural contexts.

The shared experience of countries grappling with debt obligations and the resulting austerity measures highlights a systemic issue. The focus on generating surpluses to meet debt payments constrains governments' ability to invest in their populations and economies, creating a cycle of dependency and limited growth. This economic framework, influenced by international financial institutions, shapes the fiscal policies and social outcomes of numerous African states.

st.headline: Macau, São Tomé Sign Anti-Money Laundering Accord
st.dek: The two territories will exchange financial information to combat illicit capital flows and terrorism financing.
paragraphs: Macau and São Tomé and Príncipe are set to sign an agreement to exchange financial information aimed at preventing money laundering and terrorism financing, the government of the semi-autonomous Chinese region announced. The protocol, detailed in an official bulletin, will facilitate the sharing of financial intelligence to combat money laundering, associated underlying crimes, and the financing of terrorism and weapons of mass destruction.

The memorandum of understanding will be signed with the Financial Intelligence Unit of São Tomé and Príncipe. The accord is part of Macau's broader strategy to enhance international cooperation, having already signed similar agreements with Angola, Portugal, Timor-Leste, Brazil, and Cabo Verde. Macau's Information Office, responsible for anti-money laundering efforts, is under the authority of the Unitary Police Services.

This initiative follows a period of increased scrutiny for Macau, which was identified as a global money laundering hotspot by the U.S. State Department in 2022. Despite this, Macau was recognized in 2019 as the only member of the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering to meet all international standards. In the first half of the year, Macau's casinos reported a 8.7% rise in suspicious transaction reports, totaling 2,018 filings.

st.headline: Government Expands Social Programs, Increases Aid to Vulnerable Families
st.dek: The Cadastro Social Único will now cover over 12,500 households and the Programa Família Vulnerável will assist 6,000 families.
paragraphs: São Tomé and Príncipe's social protection system is expanding to reach more vulnerable families, with the Cadastro Social Único growing from 8,000 to over 12,500 households and the Programa Família Vulnerável increasing from 5,000 to 6,000. This expansion, financed by the World Bank, aims to reduce poverty, which affects more than half of the population. Beneficiaries like Uilza Nascimento, a single mother, have seen their social aid increase by 200 dobras, enabling her to strengthen her izaquente business and better support her children.

In addition to increased financial aid, the initiative includes training programs designed to foster financial autonomy. Approximately 500 heads of households will have access to entrepreneurship and technical training, such as product transformation, to help them create their own employment opportunities. Núria de Ceita, Director of Social Protection, Solidarity and Family, announced the expansion and highlighted the goal of empowering individuals to achieve financial independence.

The expansion of these social programs is a key strategy in addressing extreme poverty, which currently impacts around 12,500 São Toméan families, representing 25% of the population. The government's efforts, supported by international funding, focus on providing both direct assistance and skills development to improve livelihoods and reduce the national poverty rate.

sn.headline: National Assembly postpones Prime Minister's policy statement
sn.dek: The National Assembly cited procedural confusion and conflicting dates for delaying the Prime Minister's scheduled address.
paragraphs: Senegal's Prime Minister Al Aminou Lô will not deliver his policy statement on September 1 as initially planned. The National Assembly announced the postponement in a statement on Friday, August 28, 2026, citing several procedural "confusions" and issues with the proposed dates. The original plan involved the Prime Minister addressing the assembly on September 1, a date that had been set by presidential decree.

The Assembly's Bureau stated that the executive branch demonstrated a lack of understanding of parliamentary procedures. The Prime Minister had communicated his availability for September 1 to the Assembly President on August 24. However, a presidential decree issued on August 25 convened an extraordinary session starting September 1 at 10 a.m., with the Prime Minister's statement as the sole agenda item, but without specifying an exact time.

The Assembly noted that the ordinary session had closed on June 30, meaning any meeting required a decision from the President of the Republic. The Bureau attributed the discrepancies to the executive's unfamiliarity with parliamentary protocols, leading to the current uncertainty surrounding the policy statement's delivery and the assembly's calendar.

sn.headline: Mbaye Agrees Aston Villa Transfer for 55 Million Euros
sn.dek: Senegalese international Ibrahima Mbaye is moving from Paris Saint-Germain to Aston Villa in a deal valued at approximately 55 million euros.
paragraphs: Ibrahima Mbaye will depart Paris Saint-Germain to join Aston Villa, with an agreement in principle reached between the clubs for a transfer estimated at 55 million euros. The 18-year-old winger, who has been with PSG since 2018, was also of interest to Liverpool. Aston Villa accelerated their pursuit of Mbaye after failing to secure Rafael Leao, who moved to Galatasaray. The relationship between Villa owner Nassef Sawiris and PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi reportedly aided the deal's finalization.

Mbaye, who has represented Senegal internationally since November 2025, quickly became a key player for the national team. He participated in six matches during Senegal's victorious 2025 Africa Cup of Nations campaign. His performance continued at the 2026 World Cup, where he started three games and scored against France, becoming the youngest African player to score in that competition.

sn.headline: Multi-vehicle crash paralyzes AIBD-Dakar highway
sn.dek: A major pile-up involving twenty-three vehicles closed the toll road between the airport and Dakar, causing a four-kilometer traffic jam.
paragraphs: A significant collision on the AIBD-Dakar toll highway on Friday, August 28, 2026, has completely blocked traffic. The accident, which occurred around 10:25 AM near Sébi Kippi village, involved twenty-three vehicles and resulted in four serious injuries. Authorities reported a traffic backup stretching nearly four kilometers by 11:30 AM, significantly hindering emergency response efforts.

The incident forced the closure of the highway section between Toglou and Sébikotane. Traffic regulation services are advising drivers heading from AIBD or the Segea highway network to use exit 13 and reroute via the National Road. Motorists are urged to exercise caution and consider postponing or adjusting their travel plans in the affected area.

The scale of the pile-up and the resulting congestion are complicating the work of intervention and rescue teams. The full impact on travel and logistics remains unclear, but the immediate effect is a complete halt to traffic flow on this vital artery connecting the international airport to the capital city.

sn.headline: Fugitive Arrested After 23 Years for 2003 Fatal Shooting
sn.dek: Youssouph Sané, wanted for a 2003 accidental shooting that killed a 17-year-old girl, was apprehended in Baghagha after nearly two decades on the run.
paragraphs: Gendarmerie investigators in Ziguinchor have apprehended Youssouph Sané, who had been a fugitive for nearly 23 years in connection with a 2003 fatal shooting in Mandégane. Sané was arrested in the village of Baghagha, in the Tobor area, following a lengthy investigation. The incident occurred during a traditional ceremony where firearms were prohibited, but Sané allegedly handled his hunting rifle, resulting in an accidental discharge.

The accidental shot fatally struck 17-year-old Siré Goudiaby, niece of former deputy Bakary Diédhiou, who died at the scene. After the tragedy, Sané fled to Guinea-Bissau, where he lived for several years before returning to the region, moving through various locations including Kolda, before settling in Baghagha with family. Investigators tracked him to a tavern after a 24-hour surveillance operation.

During interrogation, Sané reportedly admitted to firing his weapon but maintained the shot was accidental. He was taken to Mandégane on August 27, 2026, for an investigation that included hearing testimony from about ten individuals and a reenactment of the events. The investigation continues to clarify the circumstances surrounding Goudiaby's death in September 2003.

sn.headline: Dakar's Corniche West Reclaims Public Space
sn.dek: Commercial activities have been cleared from Dakar's western Corniche, restoring the oceanfront promenade for walkers and athletes ahead of the Youth Olympics.
paragraphs: Dakar's western Corniche is regaining its former glory as a public space, with the removal of commercial stalls opening up the area for pedestrians and sports enthusiasts. This transformation, occurring weeks before the "Dakar 2026" Youth Olympic Games, allows residents to move more freely along the oceanfront. Joggers, walkers, and those using the sports equipment now find the promenade more accessible and pleasant, enjoying the sea breeze and a healthier environment for physical activity.

Residents like Amsatou Ndiaye, a teacher, express joy at the renewed beauty and clean air of the Corniche, noting its improved health benefits for exercise. Seynabou Sall and Absa Gomis also appreciate the space for their regular walks, highlighting the convenience of being outdoors by the sea. The area is no longer just a thoroughfare but a vital zone for recreation and fitness, offering a free alternative to gyms in a densely populated city.

Younger users, such as Abdou Seck and Thiaba Sambe, observe that the space feels more open and is increasingly used for sports. Sambe finds it practical to exercise there after work without cost. The revitalization of the Corniche west signifies a return to its function as a public area for mobility, physical activity, and relaxation, providing a much-needed breathing room for the city's inhabitants.

sl.headline: Charcoal burning deforests Sierra Leone, threatens food security
sl.dek: The practice, driven by limited energy access, leads to habitat loss and the cutting of economic trees, according to environmental officials.
paragraphs: Charcoal production in Sierra Leone is accelerating deforestation and environmental degradation, as limited access to electricity and clean cooking options forces many to rely on burning wood. This practice, common in Freetown and other urban centers, involves cutting down trees, including valuable fruit-bearing species, leaving land exposed and threatening biodiversity. Environmental Protection Agency Director Paul Lamin noted that the slow regrowth of trees exacerbates the problem, impacting carbon reduction efforts.

The burning of wood for charcoal and its subsequent use as an energy source releases significant greenhouse gases, contributing to air pollution and climate change. Experts estimate that traditional wood energy accounts for a substantial portion of global anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. The Food and Agricultural Organization warns that continued unsustainable charcoal production will worsen climate change, potentially reducing future wood-energy supplies.

For many families, like that of 65-year-old Pa Alimamy, charcoal burning is a primary source of livelihood, with his entire family depending on it. Despite the acknowledged environmental hazards, the government's National Energy Compact indicates that only 36% of the population has access to electricity and a mere 15% have access to clean cooking, highlighting the scarcity of viable alternatives for households unable to afford gas or electricity.

sl.headline: Sierra Leone Vice Presidents Fail to Reach Presidency
sl.dek: The office, constitutionally powerful, has historically served as a political cul-de-sac rather than a path to the presidency.
paragraphs: The Vice Presidency in Sierra Leone, though constitutionally second only to the presidency, has consistently failed to produce a successor president. Analysis suggests the office is often used for political balancing, regional appeasement, or neutralizing rivals, rather than cultivating future leadership. This practice has left many Vice Presidents without a clear succession pathway or an independent political base, hindering their presidential ambitions.

Historical examples illustrate this pattern. Sorie Ibrahim Koroma and Francis Minah, powerful insiders under Siaka Stevens, never became president, with Minah facing execution after a failed coup. Solomon Ekuma Berewa, considered highly prepared, lost decisively in 2007, demonstrating that competence in office did not guarantee electoral success. Victor Bockarie Foh's brief tenure and Samuel Sam-Sumana's estrangement and political isolation further highlight the office's limitations.

The current Vice President faces a historical precedent where the office has been a political liability rather than an advantage. The electorate's desire for change, even over experience, has repeatedly thwarted Vice Presidents' presidential bids. This recurring outcome raises questions about whether the current Vice President's fate is already sealed by this established political dynamic.

sl.headline: Women mining for income face rape and harassment
sl.dek: Artisanal miners in Kono district recount sexual assaults and community stigma after seeking income in abandoned pits.
paragraphs: Women in Sierra Leone's Kono district are facing sexual violence and harassment while working in abandoned mines, a dangerous occupation they turned to for income after the civil war. Janet, 32, recounted being raped at 15 while scavenging for diamonds and gold in Jaiama Nimikor, an experience that led to an unplanned pregnancy and community stigma. She now sends limited support to the child raised by a relative.

Haja, 48, a widow with three children, also shared her experience of being raped in the mines after her husband's death. She fled her community due to shame, leaving her children behind. When she reported the assault, the camp master dismissed her claims, suggesting the perpetrator might have been her boyfriend, which she denied.

These women, like many others, turned to mining as one of the few available avenues for income following the end of the civil war. The perilous work in abandoned pits, often undertaken alone, exposes them to significant risks, including sexual assault and a lack of recourse when reporting such incidents.

sl.headline: Finance Minister's Policies Withstand Global Shocks, Report Claims
sl.dek: A consortium's call for the finance minister's dismissal is flawed, confusing hardship with mismanagement, according to an analysis.
paragraphs: A statement by the "CSOs Consortium on Public Accountability" demanding the dismissal of Finance Minister Sheku Ahmed Fantamadi Bangura has been labeled a "deeply flawed intervention" that conflates economic hardship with mismanagement. The analysis argues that global shocks like the COVID-19 pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war, and aggressive monetary tightening significantly impacted economies worldwide, leading to inflation exceeding 20-30 percent in many Sub-Saharan African nations.

Despite these global pressures, Sierra Leone, unlike Ghana, Zambia, Nigeria, and Kenya, did not default on its debt, maintained its IMF program, and preserved access to financing. This outcome, the analysis contends, is a direct result of disciplined macro-fiscal management under Minister Bangura. Data from the Bank of Sierra Leone shows inflation peaked due to global shocks but subsequently declined through coordinated fiscal and monetary tightening, with central bank financing of deficits curtailed.

The consortium's claims of "poor inflation control" and "reckless debt accumulation" are disputed by IMF and World Bank data. While Sierra Leone remains at high risk of debt distress, its debt is predominantly concessional, commercial borrowing has been restrained, and debt management reforms have improved transparency. The analysis highlights the absence of Eurobond exposure, hidden debt, or debt-fueled spending, attributing the minister's resistance to unchecked borrowing for subsidies and wage hikes as crucial to avoiding default.

sl.headline: SLEWRC Revenue Jumps to NLE 7.4 Million
sl.dek: The Sierra Leone Electricity and Water Regulatory Commission more than tripled its internal revenue from levies and licenses in 2024 compared to the previous year.
paragraphs: The Sierra Leone Electricity and Water Regulatory Commission (SLEWRC) reported a significant increase in revenue generation, reaching NLE 7.4 million in 2024 from NLE 2.3 million in 2023. This growth stems from levies and licenses collected by the commission, which regulates electricity and water service providers. Despite not receiving budgeted funds from the Ministry of Finance for recurrent expenditures in both 2023 and 2024, SLEWRC achieved key deliverables.

In 2023, SLEWRC sanitized the packaged water industry through monitoring and enforcement, leading to more licenses and improved service quality. The commission resolved an average of eighty percent of complaints within a week and took enforcement actions against sixty-four non-compliant water companies. For 2024, SLEWRC expanded its operational network and developed a Multi-Year Tariff Order model for solar mini-grids, even without receiving allocated funds for recurrent expenditures.

Looking ahead to FY 2025-2027, SLEWRC plans to strengthen its organizational capacity, ensure market entry and universal access, and maintain international quality standards. The commission also intends to roll out a safety and warranty batching system for water products and monitor tariff rate implementation for sustainability. SLEWRC submitted a budget of NLE 5,590.29 for FY 2025 to 2027.

so.headline: Turkey Expands Somalia Security Role After Arms Ship Hijacking
so.dek: Ankara is providing support to Somali authorities following the seizure of a vessel carrying Turkish arms, while its naval presence sparks a dispute with Puntland.
paragraphs: Turkey has intensified its security engagement in Somalia, deploying warships and offering assistance after pirates seized a vessel carrying Turkish arms and equipment. Two Turkish naval ships are scheduled to visit Djibouti next week as part of this expanded mission, which aims to support Somali authorities in combating piracy and terrorism. Turkish officials have not disclosed the specific nature of their support or identified the hijacked vessel, but the move underscores Turkey's significant role in Somalia's security framework.

The seized vessel, the Cameroon-flagged LUTUF, was taken on August 17 off Puntland's coast and reportedly carries Turkish weapons, communications gear, and satellite systems destined for a Turkish military training facility in Mogadishu. The ship's 10-member crew includes nationals from India, Turkey, Georgia, and Serbia. Pirates are reportedly demanding approximately $2 million for the ship's release, though it remains unclear if negotiations have commenced.

The hijacking has also led to a diplomatic dispute, with Puntland accusing Turkey of conducting deadly air strikes near the hijacked ship's location. Puntland's Deputy Security Minister claimed these strikes killed at least 13 people, also implicating Somalia's federal government, though no verifiable evidence was provided. Neither Turkey nor any other government has claimed responsibility for the air strikes.

so.headline: Uganda Army Chief Orders Troop Withdrawal From Somalia by August 2027
so.dek: General Muhoozi Kainerugaba announced the complete pullout, ending nearly two decades of military presence amid mission funding crises.
paragraphs: Uganda will withdraw all its troops from Somalia by August 1, 2027, announced General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Uganda’s army chief. The declaration marks the end of nearly twenty years of Ugandan military involvement in the fight against al-Shabab. This announcement comes at a critical juncture for the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), which is already grappling with a funding shortfall after the United States stated it would cease UN logistics support from 2027.

Kainerugaba, son of President Yoweri Museveni, stated on social media that no Ugandan soldiers would remain in Somalia after the deadline. The timing of this announcement follows a summit hosted by Uganda for AUSSOM troop-contributing countries, where leaders appealed for continued international support and steady funding. The United States has informed the African Union that it will not fund the mission’s logistics and support services past December 31, 2026, raising concerns about AUSSOM's operational capacity.

The planned withdrawal and the funding crisis raise significant questions about AUSSOM's future and Somalia's ability to assume its own security responsibilities. The UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) is preparing to wind down operations, auctioning equipment and laying off staff. This situation intensifies concerns about whether Somali forces are prepared to secure the country independently or if the withdrawal will create an opportunity for al-Shabab.

so.headline: Somalia, Neighbors Boost Red Sea Maritime Security Cooperation
so.dek: Regional officials met in Nairobi to enhance information sharing and coordination against shared maritime threats in vital shipping lanes.
paragraphs: Security officials from Somalia, Ethiopia, Yemen, and Djibouti convened in Nairobi for a two-day dialogue focused on strengthening maritime law enforcement in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. Facilitated by the UN Office on Drugs and Crime with support from the European Union, INTERPOL, the International Maritime Organization, and IGAD, the meeting emphasized improving information-sharing, coordination, and cooperation among nations facing common maritime dangers.

The talks occurred during a period of heightened maritime tensions in the Middle East, which officials stated are impacting security in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. According to Abdurrahim Muhammad Ali of the Djibouti Maritime Authority, attacks on freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz indirectly affect the Gulf of Aden by diverting global maritime forces, potentially enabling pirates to increase their activities in the region.

The Red Sea and Gulf of Aden represent a critical global maritime corridor, vital for connecting regional economies to international markets. Disruptions in this area can significantly impact shipping routes, supply chains, and the movement of goods worldwide. Mostafa Elbanna, UNODC's Regional Coordinator, highlighted the region's complex and interconnected maritime challenges.

so.headline: Hijacker claims US citizenship, disputes cargo on M/V LUTUF
so.dek: A man identifying as a pirate aboard the seized M/V LUTUF claims to be a US citizen and disputes official accounts of the ship's cargo.
paragraphs: A man claiming to be a US citizen and part of the group holding the M/V LUTUF cargo ship off Somalia's coast has disputed official reports about the vessel's contents. The Cameroon-flagged ship, seized on August 17, is reportedly carrying weapons, armored military vehicles, and cement, according to the hijacker, contradicting claims by Somali officials and the ship's owners that it was carrying weapons, communications, and satellite equipment for a Turkish military training facility in Mogadishu.

The individual, who spoke to local media, stated that the weapons were destined for mercenary groups rather than the Turkish base. He also alleged that Somali parliament speaker Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur had contacted the pirates directly, questioning why a Somali official would negotiate if the cargo belonged to Turkey. These claims have not been independently verified, and the man's identity and nationality remain unconfirmed.

The hijacker also stated his intention to return to the United States after receiving his share of the ransom, vowing to give 90 percent of it to the poor. The interview occurred amidst a series of unclaimed airstrikes in the region following the hijacking, including an August 18 strike that killed four men near Garmaal and another on August 24 that killed at least nine people in the Jiifle area.

so.headline: Turkey's Somalia Oil Drilling Nears Early Completion
so.dek: Somali Petroleum Authority Director General Abdulkadir Adan stated that deep-sea oil and gas exploration drilling off Somalia's coast is ahead of schedule and may finish.
paragraphs: Türkiye’s deep-sea oil and gas exploration drilling off the coast of Somalia is progressing ahead of schedule and could be completed by the end of September, according to Somali Petroleum Authority Director General Abdulkadir Adan. The drilling has reached approximately 3,000 meters and is proceeding rapidly without technical difficulties. The operation, initially slated for October completion, might finish a month earlier due to the current pace.

The exploration is being conducted at the Curad-1 well, located about 370 kilometers offshore from Mogadishu, using Türkiye’s seventh-generation ultra-deepwater drillship Çağrı Bey. The project aims to drill to a total depth of 7,500 meters, with a target of 4,000 meters below the seabed. This marks Türkiye’s first deep-sea exploration drilling outside its own territorial waters.

Between 470 and 480 personnel are involved in the operation aboard the drilling and support vessels, with Turkish nationals comprising about 20 percent of the workforce. The Çağrı Bey is supported by the Altan, Korkut, and Sancar vessels, and Turkish naval assets are providing security for the fleet. No accidents or technical problems have been reported thus far.

ss.headline: South Sudan struggles with voluntary blood donations
ss.dek: The World Health Organization warns that low voluntary blood donation rates risk patient lives due to unstable supply.
paragraphs: South Sudan faces significant challenges in transitioning from family and replacement blood donors to voluntary contributions, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Low voluntary non-remunerated blood donations, ranging from 7.6 to 34 percent, force health facilities to rely on family members during urgent patient needs. This dependency creates an unstable supply, potentially endangering lives, especially for women in childbirth, anemic patients, trauma victims, and those undergoing surgery.

A national assessment identified critical issues hindering blood transfusion services, including inadequate infrastructure, poor storage capacity, unreliable electricity, and weak cold-chain systems. Shortages of essential equipment, insufficient trained personnel, weak quality management, and fragmented paper-based data systems further complicate efforts. The Muslim community in Juba has been noted as a primary source of voluntary donations, with mosques being the most reliable source for restocking the national blood bank.

The National Blood Transfusion Service (NBTS) aims to collect 160,000 units annually, but current voluntary donations only meet about 34 percent of this target. This deficit means lives are lost due to insufficient blood supply. Health officials are urging all faith groups, civil society, and citizens to participate in regular voluntary blood drives to bridge the gap and ensure adequate blood availability for medical needs.

ss.headline: Communal clashes kill 49 in South Sudan cattle camp
ss.dek: Renewed fighting erupted Thursday morning at a cattle camp in Tonj North County, leaving dozens dead and wounded, according to local authorities.
paragraphs: At least forty-nine people were killed and thirty-three others injured in renewed communal clashes in Tonj North County, Warrap State, local officials reported. The violence occurred around 5:00 AM on Thursday at the Machar-Pakuek cattle camp and Mading Juer Boma in Majak Payam. William Wol Mayom of the Warrap State Ministry confirmed the casualties.

In a separate incident, two people were killed in an ambush on the outskirts of Jebel Boma County, according to the Minister of Information for the Greater Pibor Administrative Area. Unidentified attackers ambushed and killed the two individuals before fleeing the scene. Security forces have been dispatched to investigate the attack and identify the perpetrators.

Preliminary investigations into the Jebel Boma ambush suggest the attackers may have come from the direction of Kuron in Kapoeta East County, Eastern Equatoria State. Authorities in Kapoeta East County and the Eastern Equatoria State government have not yet commented on the incident. The circumstances surrounding both attacks remain unknown.

ss.headline: Prosecutors deny singling out Machar in trial procedure dispute
ss.dek: The Special Court prosecution argued that its application seeks to apply correct legal procedure to all defendants, not to treat the suspended First Vice President differently.
paragraphs: Prosecutors at the Special Court in Juba stated Friday that their counter-application does not aim to single out suspended First Vice President Dr. Riek Machar. Lead prosecutor Ajo Ony’Ohisa argued during the 113th proceeding that the application seeks clarification and prospective application of statutory procedure to all remaining defendants. The prosecution emphasized it does not intend to invalidate or reopen completed examinations or subject Machar, the fifth accused, to different treatment.

The prosecution cited Section 197(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, which allows the court to question an accused person at any stage to explain circumstances appearing in evidence. They argued that the court should lead this examination by putting material circumstances from prosecution evidence to the accused, who can then explain, deny, or decline to answer. This contrasts with the defense's apparent desire for defendants to read prepared statements first.

The defense, led by Dr. Geri Raimondo Legge, objected to the prosecution's use of a rejoinder, describing it as misleading. The court adjourned proceedings until September 7, 2026, when it is expected to rule on the defense's application for clarification of legal representation rights and the prosecution's counter-application. Machar and seven others face trial over violence in Nasir in March 2025.

ss.headline: South Sudan Mothers Breastfeed Less Than Half of Babies Exclusively
ss.dek: Only 71% of mothers in South Sudan exclusively breastfeed their babies during the first six months of life, according to recent data.
paragraphs: Exclusive breastfeeding rates in South Sudan fall short of optimal levels, with only 71% of mothers providing only breast milk to their infants for the first six months. This figure comes from UNICEF and health-sector data, highlighting a significant portion of mothers not meeting recommended exclusive breastfeeding practices.

Despite the lower exclusive breastfeeding rate, the data indicates a strong initiation trend. A substantial 76% of mothers in South Sudan begin breastfeeding their babies within the first hour after birth, according to the 2025 MICS survey. However, the continuation of exclusive breastfeeding drops to 71% until the child reaches two years of age.

The findings underscore a gap between the early initiation of breastfeeding and its sustained exclusive practice throughout infancy. Health organizations emphasize the critical role of exclusive breastfeeding for infant health and development, suggesting challenges in maintaining this practice beyond the initial hours after birth.

ss.headline: Red Cross Distributes Aid to Displaced South Sudanese
ss.dek: Humanitarian aid reached 1,700 households in Kajo-Keji County, providing food and essential services to those displaced by recent border clashes.
paragraphs: The International Committee of the Red Cross and South Sudan Red Cross began distributing humanitarian assistance in Kajo-Keji County to individuals who returned from Ugandan refugee camps and local residents displaced by fighting last month. The distribution on Wednesday reached 1,700 of the targeted 2,600 households, with aid deliveries completed in Mangalatore, Keriwa, and Sokare. The aid includes food, rehabilitation of water boreholes, and family-linking services.

Renewed fighting in mid-July 2026, reportedly involving UPDF troops crossing into South Sudanese territory, resulted in multiple fatalities and displaced an estimated 16,000 civilians. Local community leaders expressed gratitude for the relief efforts, noting that poor road conditions had caused significant logistical delays. They also called for expanded registration to accommodate new arrivals.

Beneficiaries highlighted that current aid allocations often fall short for larger households, with some families of up to 14 members receiving insufficient supplies. They urged aid agencies to adjust distribution quantities based on verified family sizes. The support is seen as crucial for vulnerable groups, including children, women, and the elderly, bringing hope and dignity to the affected community.

sd.headline: Displaced in Nyala Face Critical Shortages Amid Rainy Season
sd.dek: Hundreds of families in South Darfur shelters lack food, water, medicine, and adequate shelter as rains worsen conditions.
paragraphs: Emergency rooms and health centers in Nyala, South Darfur, report a critical decline in humanitarian conditions across displacement shelters. Hundreds of families face inadequate basic needs, including severe shortages of food, water, medicines, shelter materials, and hygiene supplies. Nibras Abdullah, a member of Nyala’s emergency room, stated that conditions have become extremely dire, especially with the onset of the rainy season, forcing some families to live in the open or in damaged classrooms where rainwater leaks through.

Specific shelters like El Jir, housing approximately 214 families, are in urgent need of food, water, and shelter materials, along with repairs to toilets and secure fencing. El Hamaira shelter, with about 274 families, requires immediate supplies of food, water, hygiene items, and medicines, particularly for chronic conditions. Other shelters, including El Zahra (115 families) and Mahira School (457 families), along with numerous others across the city, face similar widespread shortages.

While some organizations provide assistance, Abdullah described the scale of aid as insufficient compared to the growing needs. Rising prices exacerbate the difficulty in meeting demands, as the support does not match the increasing number of displaced families. Abdullah called for urgent intervention from humanitarian organizations and authorities to provide essential supplies and improve temporary accommodations to prevent further deterioration during the ongoing rainy season.

sd.headline: Sudan lifts two-year curfew and state of emergency in Khartoum
sd.dek: Authorities announced the easing of restrictions to allow residents to move and work around the clock, but security remains tight with ongoing patrols and checkpoints.
paragraphs: Sudan has lifted a two-year night-time curfew and state of emergency in the capital, Khartoum, a move authorities say will permit residents to move and work without time restrictions. The decision was announced by the Security Affairs Coordination Committee following a meeting chaired by Khartoum Governor Ahmed Othman Hamza. Despite the easing of restrictions, security remains tight with army patrols and checkpoints continuing to operate across the capital.

Residents travelling late at night are still urged to carry identification documents. Authorities have also imposed new restrictions on foreign nationals entering Khartoum State, prohibiting entry by public or private transport, including trains and buses, unless travellers possess valid visas or permits. The curfew was initially introduced in May 2024 as fighting intensified between Sudan’s army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.

Sudan’s war has been ongoing since April 2023, resulting in tens of thousands of deaths and displacing approximately 13 million people, according to UN and international estimates. Military authorities retook control of Khartoum 18 months ago, though conflict persists in other areas.

sd.headline: Fighting Disrupts Trade, Raises Famine Fears in Sudan's Kordofan
sd.dek: The Kordofan Observatory warns of imminent famine as fighting closes roads, halts aid, and drives up food prices beyond reach.
paragraphs: The Kordofan Observatory reports signs of impending famine in multiple areas, including El Nahud, Wad Banda, El Khuwei, and Muglad. Residents are resorting to ambaz, a groundnut residue normally fed to animals, as living conditions worsen, food prices skyrocket, and humanitarian aid diminishes. Testimonies indicate a severe drop in income sources, with a malwa of millet now costing 35,000 Sudanese pounds, making it unaffordable for many families.

This crisis is exacerbated by recent fighting around El Obeid and military build-ups, which have disrupted trade routes and prevented essential goods from reaching Kordofan. Farmers struggle to access and cultivate their land, compounded by a late rainy season. The observatory attributes the escalating food insecurity to continued conflict, closed trade routes, and restricted humanitarian access, warning of a potential widespread catastrophe.

The Kordofan Observatory urges warring factions to establish secure trade and humanitarian corridors and to refrain from using aid as leverage. It also calls on Khartoum and Northern State authorities to reverse transport restrictions to areas controlled by the Rapid Support Forces, which disproportionately burden civilians. The observatory further requests the Rapid Support Forces to facilitate trade and remove checkpoints contributing to inflated prices.

sd.headline: Kassala Gold Traders Strike Over Unregulated Street Vendors
sd.dek: Gold merchants in Kassala have closed their shops indefinitely, demanding authorities address fraud and market distortions caused by itinerant sellers.
paragraphs: Kassala's gold traders began an indefinite strike on Monday, shutting down their established shops to protest the growing problem of unregulated itinerant gold sellers. Abboud Ahmed Issa, head of the goldsmiths’ association, stated the strike will continue until authorities intervene to resolve issues like fraud, theft, and market distortions. He explained that established traders are held accountable for customer complaints, but unregistered vendors disappear, leaving the association to manage the fallout.

The issue, which has worsened since the Covid-19 pandemic, involves itinerant sellers engaging in practices such as manipulating gold weight, offering inflated prices, and trading without official invoices. This creates an unregulated parallel market that bypasses taxes and fees borne by legitimate shop owners. Traders report that recent confrontations between established merchants and itinerant sellers have led to injuries, prompting the current widespread closure.

Issa expressed frustration that the phenomenon damages the reputation of Kassala's gold market and creates tension. The association is calling on police, prosecutors, and security agencies to fulfill their regulatory role. They are prepared to cooperate with any official measures to protect both customers and legitimate traders, emphasizing that the strike will persist until a clear solution is implemented to ensure fair market practices.

sd.headline: South Sudan Summons Envoys Over Election Statement
sd.dek: Foreign Minister James Pitia Morgan summoned the ambassadors of Germany, Japan, Norway, and the United States to protest a joint statement urging political dialogue ahead.
paragraphs: South Sudan has summoned the ambassadors of Germany, Japan, Norway, and the United States following a joint statement that urged the country's leaders to revive political dialogue and strengthen accountability before December elections. Foreign Minister James Pitia Morgan expressed the government's concern, describing the statement as inappropriate and divisive during the election preparation period. The ministry stated that Morgan stressed the importance of national ownership and non-interference in internal affairs, suggesting sensitive political matters should be handled through diplomatic channels.

The summoned diplomats had issued their joint statement after meeting with Vice President Rebecca Nyandeng de Mabior in Juba. In their statement, they called for "urgent action" and "authentic inter-party dialogue," urging leaders to renounce violence and ensure public revenues are used for services and accountability. They suggested these steps would foster private investment, security, and the rule of law, contributing to a future of peace and prosperity.

This diplomatic summons follows recent public remarks by Vice President Nyandeng, who questioned the country's direction and the effectiveness of current leadership in improving citizens' lives. She also noted infrequent meetings with President Salva Kiir, highlighting internal political discussions that preceded the international envoys' intervention.

tg.headline: Togo Power Company Announces Scheduled Electricity Cuts Until September 21
tg.dek: The Compagnie Énergie Électrique du Togo (CEET) will implement intermittent power outages nationwide due to maintenance on the West African Gas Pipeline.
paragraphs: The Compagnie Énergie Électrique du Togo (CEET) has announced that electricity supply will be temporarily interrupted across the country from August 28 to September 21, 2026. These disruptions are attributed to scheduled maintenance work on the West African Gas Pipeline (WAGP). The CEET plans to use more expensive liquid fuels to mitigate the impact of these works on the electrical supply.

Despite these measures, the company warns that sporadic power cuts may still occur during the announced period. The CEET advises electricity consumers to take necessary precautions. Specifically, users are recommended to disconnect electrical appliances during outages to prevent potential damage from voltage fluctuations when power is restored.

The maintenance on the gas pipeline necessitates these temporary reductions in electricity provision. While the CEET is employing alternative fuel sources, the cost of these fuels is higher than usual. The company's advisory aims to help the public manage the inconvenience and protect their equipment from potential surges.

tg.headline: Police and Gendarmes Extort Motorcyclists in Lomé
tg.dek: Mixed detachments of police and gendarmes are setting up ambushes at Lomé intersections to demand payments from motorcyclists.
paragraphs: In Lomé and its suburbs, police and gendarmes are reportedly setting up ambushes at strategic times, targeting motorcyclists. Instead of directing traffic, these mixed detachments allegedly stop riders for minor or fabricated infractions, such as running red lights, overloading, or lacking helmets. In some cases, motorcycles are impounded without clear justification, with officers then offering informal settlements on the spot for immediate release.

Those who cannot pay immediately are directed to a collection site the next day, where a flat fee of seven thousand five hundred CFA francs is demanded for the motorcycle's return, regardless of whether an offense was officially recorded. This practice, often conducted without official receipts or proper legal documentation, is described as a systematic extortion enterprise rather than a security mission.

Documented incidents include a delivery rider forced to pay seven thousand five hundred CFA francs after being told to pay five thousand FCFA on the spot, leading to two lost workdays. Workers returning from factories have also reported their motorcycles sustaining damage during impoundment, with no vehicle condition report filed. Some owners who paid the arbitrary fee have found their motorcycles missing from the impound sites, with no clear record of their seizure.

tg.headline: New Group Tackles Plastic Waste in Lomé
tg.dek: ZDP-Togo launched activities to collect, recycle, and transform plastic waste, addressing pollution in waterways and food chains.
paragraphs: The association "Zéro Déchet Plastique-Togo" (ZDP-Togo) officially began its work on August 27, aiming to combat the pervasive plastic pollution that blights Lomé's streets, gutters, and coastline. Plastic bags clog waterways, packaging accumulates in markets, and microplastics are entering the food chain, posing a threat to health and the environment. ZDP-Togo's motto, "Everything transforms!", signals its commitment to finding solutions beyond simple disposal.

Gérard Djossou, President of ZDP-Togo and a municipal councilor, highlighted the health risks associated with plastic waste, including potential chronic illnesses and cancers from microplastic contamination. He urged public authorities to enforce existing environmental laws, such as the 2008 framework law and subsequent decrees and regulations, rather than creating new ones. Djossou also called on individuals to reduce consumption, avoid littering, reuse plastics, and participate in their recycling.

The organization plans to organize collection efforts, leveraging neighborhood development committees to tackle the accumulation of plastic waste in gutters and waterways, which exacerbates flooding risks in Lomé. ZDP-Togo's launch was attended by local officials, representatives from public bodies like EPAM and ANASAP, and community leaders, underscoring a collaborative approach to environmental management.

tg.headline: Togo Adopts New Forest Code and Investment Agency Decree
tg.dek: The Council of Ministers approved a revised forest code and a decree on the Agency for Investment Promotion and the Free Zone.
paragraphs: Togo's Council of Ministers, led by President Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, adopted a new forest code aimed at strengthening legal frameworks for sustainable natural resource management, climate change adaptation, and biodiversity preservation. The revised code introduces major innovations, including enhanced local governance and participation in forest resource management, redefined national forest domain categories, and strengthened provisions for the rights and interests of local communities in forest classification procedures.

The new forest code also enshrines principles for accessing genetic resources and equitable benefit-sharing, bolsters forest control, and combats illegal wildlife trade and other forest offenses. It includes incentive mechanisms for agroforestry, private investment, and the energy transition to reduce pressure on forest resources, aligning with national reforestation and protected area management policies.

Additionally, the Council adopted a decree detailing the attributions, organization, and functioning of the Agency for Investment Promotion and the Free Zone (API-ZF). This move is intended to streamline investment processes and promote economic development within designated free zones.

tn.headline: Tunisia Launches Pilot Floating Solar Study at Sidi El Barrak Dam
tn.dek: A pilot study to install floating solar panels on the Sidi El Barrak dam aims to generate electricity and reduce water evaporation.
paragraphs: Tunisia's Ministry of Agriculture launched a pilot study on August 27 to assess the installation of floating solar panels at the Sidi El Barrak dam in Béja governorate. The initiative seeks to produce electricity while simultaneously decreasing water loss through evaporation from the reservoir. The findings from this experiment will determine the feasibility of replicating this technology on other Tunisian water bodies.

This floating solar system involves placing photovoltaic panels on the surface of a water reservoir. At Sidi El Barrak, the dual purpose is to utilize existing surface area for power generation and to mitigate water loss due to evaporation. This project addresses Tunisia's growing electricity demands and the increasing pressure on its water resources, aligning with the TECH-EAU research program focused on water management and technological solutions.

The ministry emphasized that this is not yet an announcement for a full-scale solar plant construction. The current phase involves an in-depth study of the pilot site's technical, hydraulic, environmental, and economic aspects. Conclusions on the system's relevance, energy efficiency, and impact on evaporation are needed before any consideration of expanding the technology to other dams.

tn.headline: Tunisian judoka Oumaima Bdioui wins silver at Tarente 2026 Mediterranean Games
tn.dek: Oumaima Bdioui secured the silver medal in the -48kg category, marking Tunisia's first judo podium at the Games.
paragraphs: Tunisian judoka Oumaima Bdioui earned a silver medal in the under-48kg category at the Tarente 2026 Mediterranean Games. She was defeated in the final by Turkey's Tuğçe Beder. This podium adds to Bdioui's successful season, which included a victory at the Tunis African Open and a bronze medal at the African Championships. Her performance in Tarente represents the first judo medal for Tunisia in this edition of the Games.

Bdioui advanced to the final by defeating Algeria's Rahma Ghalima in the quarterfinals and Italy's Giulia Ghiglione in the semifinals. The final match concluded with a referee's decision in favor of her opponent. Bdioui stated that her opponent had studied her style and limited her attack options. Tunisian national coach Nihel Cheikhrouhou expressed satisfaction, viewing the result as excellent preparation for the upcoming World Championships in Azerbaijan.

This silver medal follows Bdioui's gold at the Tunis African Open in February and bronze at the African Seniors Championships in Nairobi in April. She also won bronze at the 2022 Oran Mediterranean Games. With this latest achievement, Tunisia now holds 15 medals at the Tarente Games: 2 gold, 4 silver, and 9 bronze.

tn.headline: Tunisian Government Restores Double Workday for Public Employees
tn.dek: State employees will return to a split workday schedule starting September 1, 2026, after a summer of reduced hours.
paragraphs: Tunisia's government announced the return to a double workday for state employees, local authorities, and administrative public institutions. This change, effective Tuesday, September 1, 2026, marks the end of the summer's single-session schedule, which was associated with decreased productivity.

The Presidency of the government issued a statement on Friday, August 28, 2026, detailing the new administrative hours. From Monday to Thursday, work will be divided into two sessions: 8:30 to 12:30 and 13:30 to 17:30. This aims to boost efficiency after the summer break.

Friday's schedule will also be split, with a morning session from 8:00 to 13:00 and an afternoon session from 14:30 to 17:30. This administrative shift is intended to re-establish a more rigorous work rhythm across public sector entities.

tn.headline: Tunisia Destroys 33,000 School Supplies for Heavy Metals
tn.dek: Authorities have removed over 33,000 non-compliant school supplies containing heavy metals from the market since the start of 2026.
paragraphs: Tunisian authorities have intensified checks on school supplies, destroying or re-exporting 33,084 items found to contain heavy metals since the beginning of 2026. Salwa Fatnassi, director of quality and consumer protection at the Ministry of Commerce, stated that these products were removed due to the presence of substances posing health risks, particularly for children. This action represents an increase from the 30,648 items previously reported as non-compliant earlier in August.

In addition to the destroyed or re-exported items, another 2,490 articles have been prohibited or seized. This separate category includes 1,926 items designed to resemble food, which present a particular risk due to their appearance. These figures highlight distinct actions taken against different types of non-compliant products entering the market.

Overall, Tunisia imported 66,257,591 school supply items since the start of the year, with approximately 90% of products sold being imported. The significant volume of imports underscores the necessity for stringent controls to ensure the safety and conformity of goods intended for students as the school year approaches.

tn.headline: Tunisian Insurers Eye Residential Solar Panel Coverage
tn.dek: A new voluntary insurance product could offer a solution for protecting growing photovoltaic investments against diverse risks.
paragraphs: Residential solar panel installations are increasingly viewed as significant patrimonial and energy investments, necessitating tailored protection. These systems, designed for decades of operation, face numerous risks including weather events, fires, electrical faults, installation defects, building damage, theft, aging, production interruptions, and third-party liability. Insurance companies are exploring this area as a potential new market, but effective coverage requires a clear understanding of the specific risks associated with each installation.

To address this, an independent risk assessment process is proposed. zm.headline: Electoral Commission Orders Fresh Mandevu By-Election After Security Breach
zm.dek: The Electoral Commission of Zambia has ordered a new parliamentary election in Mandevu following disruptions to result management during the August 13 general election.
paragraphs: The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has decided to hold a fresh parliamentary election in Lusaka's Mandevu constituency. This decision follows a significant security breach that disrupted the management of election results after the August 13 general election. The ECZ announced its resolution after concluding its review of the situation, a move that has garnered support from various civic and electoral oversight stakeholders.

The disruption occurred during the process of managing results from the August 13 general election. Details of the security breach itself were not provided, but the ECZ's decision indicates it was severe enough to compromise the integrity of the initial count. The commission's conclusion led to the order for a new election in the affected constituency.

This development comes as opposition parties urge the African Union to intervene in Zambia's disputed election, with concerns that the September 1 inauguration of President-elect Hakainde Hichilema could render scrutiny of the vote moot. The ECZ's decision to order a fresh election in Mandevu addresses a specific electoral management issue within the broader context of the general election.

zm.headline: Zambian opposition leader detained on treason charges
zm.dek: Brian Mundubile, who disputed the presidential election results, surrendered to police after two weeks in hiding.
paragraphs: Zambian opposition leader Brian Mundubile and his running mate Makebi Zulu have been taken into custody on treason allegations, police announced Thursday. Mundubile, a 55-year-old lawyer, surrendered after two weeks in hiding following a summons related to an alleged national security threat. He was the runner-up in the recent presidential election, receiving 38 percent of the vote compared to incumbent Hakainde Hichilema's 60 percent.

Mundubile had vowed to challenge the election outcome, but Zambia's judiciary was closed on Monday, the final day for filing objections, citing unspecified security reasons. International NGO Human Rights Watch called the closure a blow to due process and transparency. The Constitutional Court stated it had not received any election petitions, paving the way for Hichilema's inauguration, though the Chief Justice noted an irregular petition from a private citizen was forwarded for consideration.

Eight church mother bodies have denied negotiating a political reconciliation deal between the government and the detained opposition leaders. They stated their role was limited to facilitating Mundubile and Zulu's safe departure from United Nations premises to their lawyers. The leaders' detention follows their dispute of the election results, with Mundubile having been in hiding prior to his surrender.

zm.headline: Zambia Pursues Deeper Trade Ties With Brazil
zm.dek: Government implements reforms to lower business costs and attract Brazilian investment, seeking enhanced cooperation.
paragraphs: Zambia is actively pursuing enhanced trade and investment cooperation with Brazil, according to government officials. The Ministry of Commerce, Trade and Industry is implementing reforms designed to reduce the cost of doing business within the country. These measures aim to position Zambia as a more attractive investment destination for Brazilian companies and other international investors.

Permanent Secretary for Investment and Industrialisation, Crusivia Hichikumba, stated that the government's focus is on deepening these economic partnerships. The reforms are intended to streamline processes and create a more favorable environment for foreign direct investment. This initiative signals a strategic effort to boost bilateral trade relations and stimulate economic growth through increased collaboration.

The government's commitment to these reforms underscores its objective of making Zambia a competitive hub for international business. By addressing the cost of doing business, Zambia hopes to unlock new opportunities for trade and investment, particularly with key partners like Brazil. This proactive approach is expected to yield significant economic benefits and strengthen Zambia's position in the global marketplace.

Seven of the procedures were classified as major surgeries, addressing complex medical conditions in young patients.

The initiative aimed to alleviate the burden on local healthcare facilities and provide access to advanced surgical interventions for children who might otherwise face significant delays or lack of access to such care.

The operations conducted at Kasama General Hospital represent a significant effort to decentralize specialized medical services. This surgical camp provided essential treatment for children with various conditions, underscoring the importance of outreach programs in improving healthcare outcomes in underserved areas of Zambia.

zm.headline: Bus Truck Collision Kills Four on Great East Road
zm.dek: A head-on collision between a bus and a truck on Thursday morning in Rufunsa District resulted in four fatalities and 36 injuries.
paragraphs: Four people died and 36 were injured Thursday when a bus carrying 57 passengers collided with a truck on the Great East Road in Rufunsa District. The crash occurred around 11 a.m. in the Lukwipa area, according to the Zambia Police Service. The bus, a Zhongtong public service vehicle operated by Power Tools Company, was traveling toward Chipata. The truck, a Volvo with a trailer, was heading toward Lusaka.

Police identified the deceased as the bus driver, Ask Mulobela, and the bus conductor, Innocent Mulobela, who was also the driver's son. Both were pronounced dead at Mpanshya Mission Hospital. Thirty-five bus passengers were injured and admitted to the same hospital, along with the truck driver, Paul Banda, 25, who sustained serious injuries.

Preliminary investigations suggest the truck driver swerved into the opposite lane to avoid a stationary vehicle, leading to the head-on collision with the bus. The bus was registered as ADE 5711, while the truck and trailer were registered as AJE 4462 and ALF 7035T, respectively. The truck driver is from Sinda District.

eh.headline: Morocco Migrant Surge Follows Spanish Sahrawi Law
eh.dek: Thousands crossed into Ceuta after Spain advanced a law granting nationality to Sahrawis, a move Morocco opposed.
paragraphs: Tens of thousands of people crossed into Ceuta in late July, with official figures ranging from 50,000 to 72,000. The influx occurred within hours, following a seven-day period that saw Spain's Congress of Deputies approve a report on a bill granting Spanish nationality to Sahrawis born under Spanish administration. This legislative step, previously stalled, was agreed upon by the PSOE party, with the final vote in the Justice Commission occurring on July 23rd.

Security sources cited by El Español newspaper suggested Morocco used migration pressure as a diplomatic tool to express discontent with Spain's Sahrawi nationality law and its closer ties with Algiers. El Público newspaper described the event as Morocco transferring its displeasure over the same law to Ceuta, through a deliberate lack of border surveillance. Moroccan Minister of Justice Abdellatif Ouahbi later publicly asserted sovereignty over Ceuta and Melilla, attributing the crossing to Spain's migration policy.

The Moroccan National Council for Human Rights accused the Spanish Civil Guard of mistreating migrants. The sequence of events suggests a deliberate opening of borders, followed by denial and the use of migrants as leverage against the receiving country. The scale of the crossing is considered incompatible with the security apparatus Rabat maintains at the border, for which it receives payment from the European Union.

eh.headline: Sahrawis' Spanish Nationality Path Advances in Congress
eh.dek: A proposed law offers a special route for Sahrawis born before September 1977 to gain Spanish nationality, with descendants also eligible.
paragraphs: A bill to grant Spanish nationality to Sahrawis is moving toward a decisive phase in the Congress of Deputies after the summer recess. The Justice Commission approved a report on August 7, which will serve as the basis for the full congressional vote. This legislation establishes an exceptional pathway for individuals born in Western Sahara before September 29, 1977, to obtain Spanish nationality by decree, even if they do not currently reside in Spain.

To qualify, applicants can present various documents, including old Spanish identity cards, birth certificates, family books, or official Spanish administration records. Additionally, school certificates, pension documents, driving licenses, or medical records will be considered collectively as proof of eligibility. The proposal also extends eligibility to first-degree descendants, who will have a five-year window from their parent's nationality registration to exercise their option.

Applications for this special nationality status are expected to be accepted for a period of three years from the law's enactment. The process aims to provide a legal framework for Sahrawis with historical ties to Spain to formally acquire Spanish citizenship, acknowledging their past connections and facilitating their integration or recognition.

ls.headline: Man Sentenced to 20 Years or M15,000 Fine for Fatal Food Dispute
ls.dek: A Leribe man convicted of culpable homicide must also pay M30,000 compensation to the victim's family after a fatal altercation.
paragraphs: Masupha Katse has been sentenced to 20 years in prison or a M15,000 fine for killing ’Mane Mothatjaneng during a village celebration in August 2019. Acting High Court Judge ’Manapo Motebele also ordered Katse to pay M30,000 compensation to the victim’s family. The fatal assault occurred at Ha Seetsa following a dispute over food served at a community event.

Justice Motebele rejected Katse’s self-defense claim, finding he inflicted the fatal injury during a heat of passion after sudden provocation. The incident began when Katse, arriving from an initiation ceremony, demanded meat and papa, remarking that only dogs ate meat without the staple. A subsequent intervention by Mothatjaneng escalated into violence, with the Crown asserting Katse struck Mothatjaneng on the forehead with a stick.

Although no witnesses saw the fatal blow, prosecutors presented circumstantial evidence and alleged informal admissions. A post-mortem confirmed a severe head injury as the cause of death. The defense argued Katse struck Mothatjaneng on the chest, believing he was reaching for a concealed knife, and highlighted the deceased's violent reputation and a prior serious head injury.

ls.headline: Matekane Denies Links to Crime Boss Matlala
ls.dek: Prime Minister Sam Matekane stated he never met South African crime boss Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala, but confirmed a former aide dealt with him.
paragraphs: Prime Minister Sam Matekane has denied any association with South African crime figure Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala, who claimed to be negotiating VIP protection services in Lesotho. Matekane stated he has never met, known, or conducted business with Matlala, nor authorized any company linked to him for security services. This statement addresses prior allegations of a business partnership between the two.

The Prime Minister’s Office acknowledged that a former member of Matekane’s private security detail engaged with Matlala regarding the establishment of a VIP security company in Lesotho. However, the office insisted these discussions were in the former aide’s private capacity and without the Prime Minister’s knowledge or authorization. Matlala had testified before South Africa’s Madlanga Commission about these negotiations.

Matlala told the commission his company was registered in Lesotho and he was in talks for security services, including presidential protection. He also confirmed working with General Lesetja Senona, a Hawks provincial head, who was interested in the Lesotho venture but was ultimately not hired. The Prime Minister’s clarification aimed to distance himself directly from Matlala’s alleged dealings.

ls.headline: Mofomobe challenges drug case joinder
ls.dek: Basotho National Party leader Machesetsa Mofomobe asked the Maseru Magistrate’s Court to drop him from a M5 billion drug case.
paragraphs: Basotho National Party leader Machesetsa Mofomobe has asked the Maseru Magistrate’s Court to remove him from the M5 billion Khubetsoana drug case. Mofomobe’s lawyer, Advocate Christopher Lephuthing, argued that his client was unlawfully joined as the sixth accused while an application by his five co-accused to quash the charges was still pending. The MP is accused of facilitating premises used by Chinese nationals for a clandestine drug laboratory.

Advocate Lephuthing told Magistrate Lebusa Tšosane that the court lacked jurisdiction to join Mofomobe while the charges' validity was under challenge. He urged the prosecution to withdraw the charges, warning of a formal application if they refused. The prosecution rejected this, citing the law allowing additions at any stage before proceedings commence. Magistrate Tšosane ordered Mofomobe to file a formal challenge by August 31, 2026, to be heard with the co-accused’s pending bid.

The defence argued that prosecutors sought to join Mofomobe while pleadings for the quashing application were being finalized. They described the joinder as an abuse of court process and problematic for synchronizing remand dates. However, Crown prosecutor Advocate Keketso Motiki maintained that the Criminal Procedure and Evidence Act permits adding charges and accused persons before a case proceeds. The magistrate suggested the challenge should have been raised formally earlier.

ls.headline: Prime Minister Demands No Mercy for Drug Lords
ls.dek: Prime Minister Sam Matekane called for a tougher crackdown on drug dealers, citing the M5 billion Khubetsoana drug case.
paragraphs: Prime Minister Sam Matekane has demanded a more aggressive approach to combating drug trafficking, stating that narcotics are increasingly harming Basotho youth and communities. He emphasized that individuals involved in distributing drugs should face severe penalties from the justice system. Matekane's call comes amid the ongoing M5 billion Khubetsoana drug case, which involves three Chinese nationals, their company, a senior government official, and a political party leader charged with operating a clandestine drug-manufacturing facility.

During a visit to Mabote Police Station, Matekane highlighted the pervasive threat of drug use, which affects both young people and adults. He praised the police for dismantling a drug warehouse in Berea, expressing hope for strong court punishments for those responsible. The Prime Minister also questioned the adequacy of the recently approved 500 additional police officers in addressing the escalating drug problem, urging the Commissioner of Police to assess the situation.

The M5 billion case involves charges against Chen Wei, Chen Minglevu, Yang Xiong Kang, their company Stan Dar (Pty) Ltd, Kemong Masupha, and Machesetsa Mofomobe. They face accusations related to drug manufacturing, illegal importation of medicines, and environmental pollution. The accused deny the charges and are contesting them. The police had previously discovered approximately 7.5 tonnes of chemicals suspected for manufacturing crystal methamphetamine, ecstasy, and khat-related substances at a Khubetsoana workshop.

He praised the police for dismantling a drug warehouse in Berea, expressing hope for strong court punishments for those responsible. The Prime Minister also questioned the adequacy of the recently approved 500 additional police officers in addressing the escalating drug problem, urging the Commissioner of Police to assess the situation.

The M5 billion case involves charges against Chen Wei, Chen Minglevu, Yang Xiong Kang, their company Stan Dar (Pty) Ltd, Kemong Masupha, and Machesetsa Mofomobe. They face accusations related to drug manufacturing, illegal importation of medicines, and environmental pollution. The accused deny the charges and are contesting them. The police had previously discovered approximately 7.5 tonnes of chemicals suspected for manufacturing crystal methamphetamine, ecstasy, and khat-related substances at a Khubetsoana workshop.

ls.headline: Inspector Mofolo convicted of Constable Khetheng murder
ls.dek: A High Court judge found Senior Inspector Mathibeli Mofolo guilty of intentionally causing the death of Police Constable Mokalekale Khetheng after he was taken into custody.
paragraphs: Senior Inspector Mathibeli Mofolo has been convicted of the murder of Police Constable Mokalekale Khetheng, concluding a nearly decade-long trial. High Court Judge Charles Hungwe ruled on Monday that Mofolo unlawfully and intentionally caused Khetheng’s death after taking him into police custody on March 26, 2016. Mofolo's co-accused, Senior Superintendent Thabo Tšukulu, Inspector Mabitle Matona, and Sub-Inspector Haleokoe Taasoane, were acquitted of murder charges.

While acquitted of murder, SSP Tšukulu was convicted of being an accessory after the fact for his role in an elaborate cover-up of PC Khetheng’s killing. Inspectors Matona and Taasoane were released. PC Khetheng disappeared after being taken into police custody and his body was found the next day in a gorge with signs of violence. Justice Hungwe stated that Khetheng was taken alive into custody, deliberately omitted from records, and found dead the following day.

The court found the circumstantial case against Snr Insp Mofolo overwhelming, noting he took exclusive custody, circumvented detention records, borrowed handcuffs, and received gloves. He failed to explain these actions and provided false, evasive accounts. Justice Hungwe relied on alleged admissions of Khetheng's death and attempts to suppress evidence, stating the case did not depend on excluded interrogation material.

Mofolo's co-accused, Senior Superintendent Thabo Tšukulu, Inspector Mabitle Matona, and Sub-Inspector Haleokoe Taasoane, were acquitted of murder charges.

While acquitted of murder, SSP Tšukulu was convicted of being an accessory after the fact for his role in an elaborate cover-up of PC Khetheng’s killing. Inspectors Matona and Taasoane were released. PC Khetheng disappeared after being taken into police custody and his body was found the next day in a gorge with signs of violence. Justice Hungwe stated that Khetheng was taken alive into custody, deliberately omitted from records, and found dead the following day.

The court found the circumstantial case against Snr Insp Mofolo overwhelming, noting he took exclusive custody, circumvented detention records, borrowed handcuffs, and received gloves.
